findings.issue: DA11 (about ten times the documents, weekly snapshots) is tested only by "name no limit that the current volume already approaches". The binding limit is not named in any design document: the author's attention. Operation 7.2 budgets the author at 3 hours a week and 100 items per run, assuming 30 seconds an item. The spike estimate (simulated, not measured) is 1.5 minutes per disagreement and 58-210 author hours for the 115 pending documents alone; its three small runs work out to 1.0-1.3 minutes per item, so 100 items is about 2 hours, not 50 minutes. The only overflow valve is `deferred`, which ext 7 counts as closed.
findings.why: Derived: 58-210 hours over 115 documents is 19-70 weeks of the whole weekly budget for M2 alone. At ten times the documents the queue never drains, every milestone "accepts" a growing deferred pile, and weekly refresh competes with the backlog. The plan as written cannot reach DA11 without changing who reviews what. This decides what gets built at M3a/M3b (triage and extraction of the new documents).
findings.fix: Decide before M3a a review regime per document class and state it in Requirements. For example: full review for one-off primary documents of the strict scope; sample-only review for parser output and for context material; machine-agreed rows admitted with an explicit unreviewed flag and excluded from strict headline figures until sampled. Give each class an expected author-minutes-per-document figure (replace the 30 s default by the logged rate) and add a DA11 test of the form: weekly author minutes at 10x volume and weekly refresh, under C1. Cap the queue by rank (likelihood and confidence), and admit the remainder flagged rather than defer it.

findings.section: 1. validator rule on lines.sha256, with jetp-extraction.md 2 (Canonical member)
findings.quote: at least one retrieval of the line's document yields that snapshot
findings.issue: A living document that moves to a new address (site redesign, ministry renamed) cannot keep producing lines. `documents.url` is one canonical address. The new address is found later as a second document and folded by `same_as`. Ext 2 then says "the member already extracted" stays canonical, and ext 7 gives the new member the disposition `duplicate`. But every new weekly snapshot is yielded only by retrievals of the new member, so the validator rule above rejects any line citing it under the canonical document. A relocation is not a mirror, because the two addresses are not contemporaneous copies of the same bytes.
findings.why: Three years of weekly fetches will meet site migrations (a redesigned secretariat portal is near certain), and the dead old address would stay canonical while the live one is `duplicate` and unextractable. Discovered at M4 it forces a change to the canonical rule, the validator and the document identity model.
findings.fix: Separate address from document: a `document-addresses` table (document_id, url, valid_from, valid_to, relation: canonical, mirror, relocated_from). A retrieval of any address of a document counts as a retrieval of that document. Rewrite the canonical rule by time: among contemporaneous mirrors, the existing rule; across a relocation, both addresses are one document and continuity of statements is unbroken. Change the validator rule to "some retrieval of any address of the line's document". Add a red test with a relocated living page.

findings.section: 11. Two published dates and the freeze (with jetp-ledger-storage.md 1, documents and snapshots tables)
findings.quote: The latest publication date, as its publisher
findings.issue: A single `documents.published_date` exists, and `snapshots` has no date columns. For a living document (dashboard, project data sheet, newsletter page) the date that matters is per version: the publisher's stated update date if any, else the retrieval date. The "newest document date" of F9 is published in every release and every product but is defined only for documents a publisher dates. Undated living pages are simply ignored, and the stated date may lack a year (spike: "Ngay 27/3", year only on the masthead the scope excluded). OBS-1 asks "as of which date".
findings.why: A release could state a newest document date months older than the freshest living page it relies on (the register is frozen at M3a, extraction and release come later, and weekly snapshots follow). The book cites "as of" dates from this field. Readers cannot tell retrieved-on from published-on, so a headline cutoff would mislead.
findings.fix: Add to `snapshots` or `retrievals` an `as_of_date` with precision and a source flag (publisher-stated, inferred from the document, retrieval date only). Define the newest document date over documents by `as_of_date` where publisher-stated, and publish separately the latest retrieval date of living documents. Make the release state three dates for the collection record, not two. Require the declared scope to include the dated masthead of a series or living page, so the year is a statement.

findings.section: 2 Perimeter and 3 Relations; jetp-requirements.md F13; jetp-fusion.md 6
findings.quote: succeeds a previous edition
findings.issue: `edition_of` is the only succession relation, and it covers documents. Nothing records that one partnership, platform, secretariat or ministry succeeds another. `former_name` covers a rename, not a merger, a split or a replacement. `same_as` is an equality claim and is wrong for succession. The strict JETP scope "requires explicit attribution in the document" (F13), but no column or relation records the attribution. The partnership itself is not a class: it is a perimeter of the pledge envelope. If a partnership is folded into a country platform, rebranded, or loses a partner, a textual test for "JETP" breaks and strict and extended scope shift silently.
findings.why: Reorganisations of ministries and of partnerships are likely before 2030 (Viet Nam and Indonesia have both restructured ministries). Without a dated succession relation, an operator or ministry identity either splits (losing history) or merges by `same_as` (asserting equality that is false). F13's test cannot be run as a data property, only as a text search, which the project's own guard rule distrusts. Changing the relation list after release 1 costs a new ontology version and a recount of strict-scope figures.
findings.fix: Add a dated `succeeds` relation (party to party, perimeter to perimeter, with valid_from, and optional split or merge roles). Name the partnership as a perimeter kind with name forms in force by date, including successor platform names. Define strict scope as a `member_of` row to the partnership perimeter, justified by a line that carries an attribution naming the partnership or a recorded name form for that date. Rewrite the F13 test to assert that every strict-scope item has such a justification row.

findings.section: 6. How a release is identified (with jetp-ledger-storage.md 1 as-of rule, jetp-requirements.md F10)
findings.quote: the year and
findings.issue: A regular release is named after "the year and month of its knowledge cutoff" and a correction is `YYYY-MM-rN`. Storage defines the as-of state at K as the rows with `recorded_at` on or before K, and F10 says "a later discovery never changes an earlier result". A correction of a ledger error is a supersession row recorded after K, so a release at cutoff K never contains its own correction. The spec does not say whether `YYYY-MM-rN` keeps K (and then cannot contain the correction), or takes a new K (and then also admits every statement discovered since, so a correction release is no longer a correction).
findings.why: Corrections are the normal case for three years of publisher corrections and ledger errors. Q7, Q8 and F25 need a correction release that differs from the original by the named corrections only. Without a rule, the first correction either violates F10 or silently ships unrelated new statements. The book's pinned release (BK-2) and the change attribution of M4 (F22) both depend on the choice.
findings.fix: State that a correction release is the original input version plus the named supersession rows recorded after K (a correction overlay), with its own correction date as a fifth date and the original K unchanged. Fusion 8 should give the as-of rule two axes: knowledge cutoff K and correction-overlay set. Reword F10 and its test accordingly. The descriptor names the overlay rows. The release name suffix is an ordinal, not a cutoff.

findings.section: 9. Correction and restoration (with jetp-requirements.md N11, BK-2, Q7)
findings.quote: cited figures it changes
findings.issue: Results 9 and its check table require the editorial note of a correction to list the paper figures it changes ("three country totals and one paper figure"). Nothing in any document holds which figures papers, the climate-finance article or the book cite. N11 puts manuscripts outside the Observer. Presentation keeps the provenance index as "a build-time check, never a served file" and mentions manuscript occurrences without saying where they are registered. BK-2 wants the book's figures to stay on one release "whatever later releases say", while Q7 wants a correction to reach "every published claim it touches". The two are not reconciled.
findings.why: The check is unsatisfiable as written. The first correction after the book or article quotes the Observer will either miss the affected figure or be reported from memory. Adding a register after products have been written means reconstructing citations by hand.
findings.fix: Add a `product-citations` table (product id and version, release_id, result_id or display_id, locator in the product), kept in the ledger repository and filled from a machine-readable figure manifest that each product (paper, article, book chapter) ships. Require the manifest as the condition for citing a release in F29 metadata. Reconcile BK-2 and Q7: a correction never alters a pinned product, it raises a notice naming the affected figures in it, and the author decides whether to move. State whether this table is served.

findings.section: Organisation and vocabulary, Addresses match labels (with jetp-results.md 10)
findings.quote: `#project/<project_id>`
findings.issue: Observatory page addresses carry no release identifier. Results 10 requires that "a page of an earlier release remains readable at an address that names that release" and defers it to M4 ("at M3b, the deposit of each release suffices"). Releases are also built to be cited, and the book, articles and BK-1 cite dated statements. A URL cited at M3b (`#project/...`) will point at whatever release is live later, which contradicts "Pinned, never moving" (Results 1), and retrofitting a release segment at M4 breaks every address already cited.
findings.why: Three years of monthly releases through the same address scheme, with one book pinned to the first release. The address scheme is the one thing in the presentation that cannot change after products quote it. A stable form costs nothing now and a migration later.
findings.fix: Put the release identifier in the path from the first published release (`/<release_id>/#documents`), with a moving alias (`/current/`) that redirects. Products must cite the release-qualified form. Decide where earlier releases are hosted (the `gh-pages` branch has a size budget, so the deposit may host them) and state that addresses resolve through the release-qualified path or the persistent identifier.

findings.section: 2. Revision and 8. Knowledge time and change (with jetp-ledger-storage.md 1 adjudications)
findings.quote: the publisher correcting itself
findings.issue: Fusion 2 says the change between two publisher statements "is a judgement, which says which" (development, late report, correction), but the storage contract has no decision type for it: `adjudications.decision_type` is limited to occurrence_membership, flow_coverage, perimeter_compatibility and identity. Ontology says supersession is "never a publisher". There is no relation for a published erratum or corrigendum that corrects a named earlier line, and no document type or retrieval status for a publisher's explicit withdrawal (as against a link failure). Collection 10 checks frozen documents at M4 only for "a disappearance", so a PDF silently replaced under the same address is never seen.
findings.why: F22 (M4) attributes each changed figure between releases to a reason, including "a publisher's correction", but that can only be read from judgements recorded at the time. If they are not recorded from M3b, release 2 has nothing to attribute from. The first year of corrected publisher figures would be kept as unexplained conflicts (F6) rather than explained.
findings.fix: Add an adjudication decision_type `revision` (members: earlier and later line; verdict: development, late_report, correction, rounded_restatement) using fusion 8's reason list. Add a relation `corrects` (line to line, document to document), justified by the corrigendum's line, and a document type `erratum` and retrieval status `withdrawn_by_publisher`. At M4, hash-check frozen documents as well as checking their existence; a changed hash reclassifies the document as living and flags an unannounced revision.

findings.section: 4.2 F25 Reported errors are traced (with jetp-ledger-storage.md 1, jetp-requirements.md N13 and N2, jetp-operation.md 4)
findings.quote: Each report is recorded, answered by a judgement
findings.issue: No table or document specifies where reports are recorded. Storage lists none, and F23 requires every table to be served or named as not served. A report carries a natural person's identity (reader or publisher contact), and the ledger is public CSV in git plus a frozen public release. A publisher's own correction sent privately is not admissible (N13 excludes "private communication", F27 requires public documents), so the accepted/rejected choice of F25 has no outcome for "true, but only the publisher can say so". For the reverse direction, removal of personal data or a takedown: every release is frozen ("no byte of it is replaced"), the ledger is append-only, verbatim fields keep "everything else the publisher printed for the item" (which can include named officials and contact cells, although N2 excludes natural persons only as classes), and Operation forbids agents to rewrite published history.
findings.why: OBS-7, the outcome for publishers ("correct errors through a channel that leaves a trace"), is unbuildable without this design, and a public repository receiving reader emails raises a data-protection problem that only appears at the first real report. A publisher's takedown or an erasure request after three years of frozen releases cannot be honoured by the current rules.
findings.fix: Add a `reports` table (report_id, target kind and id, received_at, reporter class: publisher or reader, claim text, judgement link, outcome, correction release id) with reporter identity kept outside the repository and named as not served in F23. Add a third outcome: valid, awaiting a public document, with the publisher told that a public erratum is what enters the ledger. Extend N2 to verbatim fields that hold natural persons' names or contacts (not stored). Write the takedown path: which action is allowed (redaction in the next release, withdrawal at the deposit under F28, a named exception to Operation's rule on rewriting history) and who alone decides.

findings.section: 6. Known items and the recall estimate (with jetp-ontology.md 2 and jetp-ledger-storage.md 1 for country codes)
findings.quote: The list holds at least 40 items across the four countries
findings.issue: Two things that N7 and M4 say extend by data do not. (1) The known-item list is frozen, hidden, pooled across four countries, and every item found or looked up enters the register. A second campaign after M3a cannot reuse it (its items are in the register) and needs a fresh list. A fifth country has too few items for a pooled estimate. Collection 11 defers M4's coverage rules "to be written when M4 opens". (2) Country is a prose list in the ontology (`ZAF`, `IDN`, `VNM`, `SEN`, or `international`) and storage uses `GLB` for no recipient country: two spellings. `lines.country` is a single required value, so a multi-country table (IPG, donor or GFANZ reports) gets one country or the no-country code, and F13's no-sum-across-countries rule then confuses "global" with "multi-country".
findings.why: N7 promises that adding a country needs "data, not a change of design"; it would need a new estimator and a DDL change. Weekly watch after M3a has no measurable recall. The same holds for successor platforms, which multiply multi-country publishers.
findings.fix: State that a known-item list is consumed by the campaign that used it, and each later campaign or new country builds its own list (items published since the last cutoff, or a capture-recapture estimate as the stated fallback). Make the country list a closed `terms` list (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 plus one local marker for no country, one spelling in ontology and storage). Add a `line-countries` relation for multi-country statements, or state that a multi-country line carries the no-country code and is excluded from per-country counts.

findings.section: 4.5 F26 and 3.6 BK-3 (with jetp-ontology.md 5, terms table)
findings.quote: plain-language definition beside its formal one
findings.issue: F26 (M4) requires a plain-language definition beside the formal one, for the book's general readers (BK-3). The `terms` table has one `definition` column (described in ontology 5 as already plain, written for a reader of the Observatory) and a `scope_note`, so there is no second slot. Yet the book pins the M3b release for its whole writing period and must move every figure to get an M4 glossary.
findings.why: A release is frozen: adding a column later gives the book either no plain definitions or a forced release move with every figure changed. The schema change is free now and costs a revision of the ontology tables afterwards.
findings.fix: Add `plain_definition` to the `terms` columns now, tagged M3b for the terms a book chapter uses and M4 for all. Reconcile ontology 5's claim that `definition` is already plain with F26 by calling one column the formal definition.

findings.section: §10 Document classes (with §2, extraction §2 and §8, fusion §3, storage §1)
findings.quote: each issue found is its own document, linked by `edition_of`
findings.issue: Issues of a series (the 13 MOIT newsletters, pending at M2) are filed as `edition_of`. Extraction §2 makes an edition its own document whose statements are 'never merged'. Extraction §8 defines restatement only between snapshots of one document, and puts key-less pairing at 'M4 for pairing without a key'. Fusion §2 'persistence, not corroboration' also covers only snapshots of one document. So no rule says whether issue 13 repeating issue 8's list of 44 projects is a restatement or independent corroboration. Collection §5 also counts 'a new edition' as yield. The spike ran issues 8 and 13 and got 0 restatements out of 7 pairs, and 2 false pairings at 'likely' or above. Storage also gives `edition_of` two homes, a `documents` column and `relations` rows (§4).
findings.why: Changes what M2 builds for series, when published counts are doubled, and whether the ledger keeps the repeat as persistence or as corroboration. A rule that is M4 for extraction but needed at M2 for the pending series cannot be built as written.
findings.fix: Decide once, in fusion §3 (documents). Add `issue_of` (issue to series, series carrying publisher and periodicity) and keep `edition_of` for a revised version of one publication. State in extraction §8 and fusion §2 that restatement, persistence and no-added-corroboration also bind statements paired across issues and editions of one lineage. Move key-less pairing for series to M2, with the author shown each pair. Drop `documents.edition_of` so the relation has one home, in `relations`. Align collection §2, §5 and §10, and the language entry for 'edition'.

findings.section: §1 Tables and rules (lines row) vs extraction §3, §6.3, §7, §8 and requirements F1, Q4, Q9, Q17
findings.quote: country, sha256, locator, ordinal, label, classification, own_status, own_status_axis, own_sector, groups, recorded_at, notes
findings.issue: Extraction §3 requires each statement to carry '**Method and version** that extracted it', the checking reader, the checker's stance and any author decision. Requirements F1, Q4, Q9 and Q17 require the same at M2. The `lines` columns hold none of them. Storage has no table or column for dispositions (extraction §7), for the 'unpaired' record and the restatement link (§8), for rejected proposals 'recorded with its reason' (§6.3), or for the reader and checker calls. `documents` has no column for the class the collection rules assign, and there is no table for triage outcomes, verdicts, the round log, the known-item list or the tracker claims. The record of searches is `dry-searches | as today`.
findings.why: The M2 checks of F1, F2, Q4 and Q17 cannot be met by the M2 tables. Ledger state that the extraction rules call the record would have no home, and the acceptance counts would rest on files outside the schema.
findings.fix: Add to storage §1, tagged M2: method, method_version and decided_by on `lines`, plus a `dispositions` table (kind, scope, reason, decided_by, method, version, recorded_at, supersedes). Add a per-statement reading-record table or rows (reader, checker, stance, likelihood, confidence, basis, author decision, step at fault). Add a link row for restatement and unpaired. Tag M3a tables for triage, class, verdicts, rounds, known items and claims, with the collection fields they must hold.

findings.section: §4 Matching records (decision rows) vs fusion §3 The judgement, and extraction §6.3, collection §9
findings.quote: `method_version`, `confidence`, `justification_line_ids`, `decided_at`,
findings.issue: Fusion §3 defines a judgement as 'a stance (the same, different, or undetermined), its likelihood and confidence', the statements it rests on, a quoted basis, who, method, version and when. Extraction §6.3 and collection §9 copy that shape for the checker and for triage. The decision rows hold a single `confidence` and no stance, likelihood or quoted basis. `adjudications` holds only verdict and status, with no method or confidence. Yet results §2 needs thresholds on likelihood and confidence for occurrence, coverage and compatibility judgements. Document duplicate judgements are M2, and they sit in `relations`.
findings.why: A match threshold such as 'likely or more, medium confidence or more' cannot be applied to a row that stores one undefined confidence. Q5 and Q11 cannot be tested at M2 for document judgements, and at M3b for occurrence, coverage and compatibility decisions.
findings.fix: Give every decision row the same columns: stance, likelihood, confidence (two separate scale values), basis_quote, method, method_version, decided_by, decided_at. Add them to `adjudications` as well. Say in storage §4 that triage outcomes and the checker's per-row stance use the same shape, and where they are stored.

findings.section: §1 Every held document accounted for, §2, §7 vs collection §2 and language (D1)
findings.quote: Every held document accounted for.
findings.issue: Collection §2 and the language document define 'held' as 'admitted and at least one of its retrievals yielded a snapshot'. Extraction §1 and §7 apply 'held' to every document 'the ledger holds' and give it the disposition `no_snapshot`, described as 'the ledger holds no bytes for it'. Requirements F2 and DA2 say 'registered' and count 392 documents, of which 23 have no snapshot. Under the defined meaning of 'held', the 23 are outside extraction's completeness rule. Also, the pending list is 'snapshots ... that have neither statements nor a disposition', but `duplicate`, `translation_not_canonical`, `out_of_scope` and `no_snapshot` are dispositions of documents, so a duplicate's snapshot never leaves the pending list.
findings.why: It decides which set the M2 acceptance count covers (392 or 369), and whether F5's test 'the pending set contains exactly it' can hold.
findings.fix: Use 'registered' (admitted) in extraction §1, §7 and §10, and keep 'held' for having a snapshot. State in §2 that a document-level disposition closes all the document's snapshots for the pending list.

findings.section: §3 Ordinal vs §1 Append only, §9, and storage §1 (line_id)
findings.quote: **Ordinal**: the statement's position within its sequence in the snapshot,
findings.issue: The ordinal is the reading-order position counted from one, and extraction §1 says an extraction 'never edits, deletes or renumbers'. Extraction §9 and storage §1 append an item missed by a re-extraction 'under the next ordinal'. A missed item that sits in the middle of the reading order must then either take a duplicate or out-of-sequence ordinal, or force a shift of later ones. Storage also mints `line_id` as `<document_id>-<table>-<ordinal>`, so the identifier's suffix and the `ordinal` column can now differ. The spike also found no defined ordinal for prose.
findings.why: Replay (Q1), idempotence (Q2) and the pair (sha256, locator) all depend on it. The code will choose one reading, and the other documents will then be wrong.
findings.fix: Say that `ordinal` is the order of admission within the snapshot and is never reassigned, and that reading order is carried by the locator. Or add a separate immutable `reading_position`. State that the `line_id` suffix is a mint counter, not the ordinal. Fix the ordinal's meaning for prose.

findings.section: §8 Access ladder and §11 M2 before the campaign vs requirements F27, C6, operation §10, storage §1
findings.quote: It may retry, on the access
findings.issue: Collection §11 lets M2 retry the 23 snapshot-less documents 'on the access ladder', but the ladder (§8), public-access-only (§1) and crawler rules (§1) are all tagged [M3a]. Operation §10 tags 'the rungs' M3a and only the 'record of an attempt' M2. Requirements put F27 at M2 and C6 at M3a. The rung vocabulary differs across documents: collection has five rungs, including an automated browser and a web archive copy; storage's `collection_method` has four values (script, browser-session, browser-manual, local-record) with no automated-browser or web-archive value; operation names two rungs. Extraction §5 says a rendered capture is 'a separate snapshot', while collection §2 keeps it 'beside' the response, and no table supports that.
findings.why: M2 performs real fetches, so its retry rules cannot be M3a. The retrieval record cannot state the rung used (collection §8) with the column as defined.
findings.fix: Tag public access, crawler rules, position recording and rungs 1 to 5 [M2] in collection, C6 and operation §10, or restrict M2 retries to rungs 1 and 2 and say so. Replace `collection_method` with the five rung names. State that a rendered capture is its own retrieval and snapshot.

findings.section: §1 documents columns vs requirements F27
findings.quote: country, document_type, language, title, url, published_date, edition_of, active, notes
findings.issue: F27 (M2) requires that 'Every document records its public access route': the address, or the public archive record, and for a registration site the free registration used. A check must fail if any document lacks one, and no route may contain a credential. `documents` holds only `url`. There is no column or table for an archive record or a registration, and operation and collection name none. The language document defines 'public access route' but no table carries it.
findings.why: The F27 check at M2 (whole register, zero documents without a route) cannot be written against the schema. For a mirror-only or archive-only document, `url` is the wrong thing to check.
findings.fix: Add an `access-routes` table (document_id, route_kind: address, archive_record or registration, value, recorded_at) to storage §1 [M2], with the validator rule: every registered document has at least one route and no value matches a credential pattern.

findings.section: §8 N4 vs collection §9 Checking at M3a, operation §4, requirements F7
findings.quote: **N4. No automatic truth.** No program admits a document, merges two
findings.issue: N4 and F7 say no program admits a document, merges identities or prefers a value, and operation §4 forbids agents to 'Admit a document'. But collection §9 says 'Where both agree, the triage outcome is in force': two LLM readers admit a document, the author sees only disagreements and a sample, and the outcome 'counts, for yield and for the register'. Fusion §3 and Q5 likewise produce identity and preference judgements 'without the author'. The documents use 'program', 'agent' and 'recorded decision' without saying whether a checked LLM pair is an allowed decider.
findings.why: A reviewer cannot say whether the M3a admission flow meets F7 and N4. A coder cannot tell whether to gate admission on an author click.
findings.fix: Redefine in requirements: a recorded decision is a judgement made by the checked reader pair and subject to the author's sampling and override (collection §9). Rewrite N4 to forbid unchecked single-program output. Say in operation §4 that 'agents' are coding agents and that the checked judgements of §5 are not agents' admissions. Give F7's test the author-sample case.

findings.section: §6.3 Assisted reading (author review) vs §7 deferred, requirements §2.2 M2 row, operation §7.2
findings.quote: The author sees only the proposals on which reader and checker disagree,
findings.issue: 'Disagree' is the trigger for the author's review in extraction §6.3, collection §9 and operation §5, but no document defines it (the spike had to invent 'stance other than right, or likelihood below likely'). Extraction §14 leaves the sample size open, operation sets 100 items per run and 3 hours per week, and the spike projects 58 to 210 hours of author review for the 115 pending documents. A document over the budget is 'split ... or deferred', and extraction §7 says a `deferred` disposition 'closes a document for the purpose of a run's completeness'. The M2 definition is 'every document ends with statements or a recorded disposition'. M2 can therefore be met by deferring most documents. Requirements DA3 also says 'row-by-row review', while Q5 says the author examines 'a bounded share'.
findings.why: Changes what M2 delivers and what a reviewer can check. The acceptance wording is satisfiable while extracting little, and the review rule has no single definition.
findings.fix: Define disagreement once in extraction §6.3 (stance, likelihood and confidence thresholds) and point collection §9, operation §5 and fusion §3 at it. Replace 'row-by-row review' in DA3 with 'every row checked by a second LLM; the author reviews disagreements and a sample'. Add to the M2 acceptance a maximum deferred share (or a list of documents that must be extracted), and reconcile the 3 h/week budget with the measured review load.

findings.section: §6 Q5, Q9 and operation §5, vs fusion §3 Documents, storage §4, collection §2 and §9
findings.quote: *M3a* for discovery and admission judgements
findings.issue: Duplicate, edition and translation judgements of documents have four different milestones. Fusion §3 (Documents [M2]), storage §4 ('M2 for documents'), extraction §2 and F3 say M2. Collection §2 tags duplicate settlement [M3a] and §9 [M3a]. Q5 and operation §5 give M2 only 'for statements extracted' and M3b for 'identity and preference judgements'. Q9 says '*M3b* for judgements and calculations', although M2 and M3a already record judgements with method and version. Fusion's document proposer 4 (an LLM reading of remaining pairs) is M2, while storage §4 builds only tiers 1 to 3 for documents at M2.
findings.why: F3 and extraction §2 need an LLM judgement at M2 with a checker from another vendor, and the requirement tags say it is M3b. The M2 scope of the LLM work is unclear.
findings.fix: Add 'document identity judgements' to the M2 list of Q5 and operation §5, and change Q9 to 'M2 for extraction methods and document judgements, M3a for triage, M3b for the rest'. Make collection §2 say 'the judgements are fusion §3, M2; new candidates at M3a'. State in storage §4 whether document proposers 4 and 5 are M2.

findings.section: §6.3 Q20 and §3.1 OBS-7 and F25 vs presentation, operation §intro, results §10
findings.quote: **Q20. Anomalies are visible in the Observatory.**
findings.issue: Q20 (M3b) requires pending judgements and broken trails to 'appear where the author looks' in the Observatory. The requirements table sends it to 'Presentation; Operation'. Operation says 'how it shows them is the presentation's business'. Presentation has no such page, and results §10 says the Observatory 'shows exactly one release at a time' and 'computes nothing the release does not contain', which excludes the working ledger's pending state. Likewise OBS-7 and F25 (M3b) need a way for a reader to report a misreading. The table points to 'Fusion § 2; Results and releases; Operation', but fusion §2 says nothing about reports, operation has no intake, and presentation has no channel.
findings.why: Two M3b requirements and OBS-7 have no document that builds them. A static release-only site cannot show pending judgements unless an author view outside the release is specified.
findings.fix: Add to presentation a named author view (pending judgements by likelihood and confidence, unresolved trails), and say in results §10 that it is built from the working ledger and is not part of a release. Add an error-report intake (for example a public address or issue tracker linked from Methods) and its recording to presentation or operation. Correct the F25 and Q20 rows of requirements §9.

findings.section: Traceability to what is published vs requirements Q6 and results §2 Its trail
findings.quote: - **The provenance index is a build-time check, never a served file.** It is
findings.issue: Q6, the results' trail rule and the presentation's own opening paragraph say the chain 'runs both ways', and Q6's test needs each sampled statement to list the figures that use it. The claim-to-observation map that gives that reverse direction is the provenance index, which presentation says is never served. The 'read-time join over the served tables' can follow a figure down to a snapshot but cannot list the figures using a given statement unless results are keyed to the observations they used. Results §2 says it 'can be listed' without saying where.
findings.why: A reviewer cannot test the reverse half of Q6 and Q7 (list the affected figures) from a release alone, which is what C7 and Q8 require.
findings.fix: Require each release to contain a served table mapping result identifier to observation identifiers (results §4), and say that the build-time index is validated against it. Reword presentation so that 'never a served file' applies to the display-occurrence record only.

findings.section: §4 The collection record, vs requirements F9, DA9, Q10 and collection §7, §11, §12
findings.quote: The M3b release takes the first form.
findings.issue: Collection §7 and §11 say the traceability rate, the two dates, the recall estimate and the unreachable list are 'published' at M3a. F9 (M3a) tests that the two dates appear 'in the release'. DA9 says the unreachable list is 'released with the register'. But results makes M3b the first release. No document defines what M3a publishes, where, or under which identifier. Results §4's collection record lists the cutoff, the newest document date, recall and the unreachable list, but omits the traceability rate, the declared protocol, the round log and the 'stopped by cap' statement (collection §5, §12), and the terminal verdicts of every authority and listed project (F8, OBS-6, LP-4).
findings.why: The M3a acceptance products have no vehicle, and the M3b release would omit parts of what DP-1 and OBS-6 ask for.
findings.fix: State in collection §12 and results §13 that M3a produces a collection report reviewed and accepted by the author (not a release), and retag F9 and DA9 'M3a report, M3b release'. Extend results §4's collection record with the protocol, round log, verdict table, cap statement and traceability rate.

findings.section: §11 Two published dates and the freeze vs fusion §1, results §4 and §6
findings.quote: admissions and judgements count, here the date of the freeze.
findings.issue: Collection says the knowledge cutoff of fusion §1 is 'here the date of the freeze' of the register. Results §2, §4 and §6 treat the knowledge cutoff as a per-release date ('`YYYY-MM`, the year and month of its knowledge cutoff') at which statements and judgements 'admitted on or before K' count. The freeze is at the end of M3a, and all M3b extraction, reading and matching are admitted after it. A release whose K equalled the freeze date would contain none of the M3b statements.
findings.why: A builder cannot tell whether K is fixed at the freeze or chosen per release, and F10 and the release identifier depend on it.
findings.fix: Delete 'here the date of the freeze'. Say that the freeze fixes only the register's membership, and that K is declared per release at or after the discovery cutoff (results §4 already requires the discovery cutoff to be on or before K).

findings.section: §4 Occurrence vs §7 Counting and requirements F14, ontology §4
findings.quote: Signing, approval and disbursement are different measures, not successive
findings.issue: Fusion §4 says signing, approval and disbursement are 'not successive states of one chronology', but fusion §7 and F14 say 'Financial states (need, announced, memorandum, approved, signed, disbursed) form a chronology'. The state list does not match the ontology either. The ontology's money axis has `announced`, `mou`, `approved`, `signed`, `cancelled`, `withdrawn` as agreement states and `pledge`, `commitment`, `disbursement`, `expenditure` as flows. 'Need' and 'memorandum' are not terms, and F19, results and language use 'reported', which is in neither list.
findings.why: F14's test ('no released figure adds signed and disbursed amounts') and the gap computations of F19 need one closed list of selectable states and one rule. As written, two rules give opposite answers.
findings.fix: Reword §4 to say that an occurrence is not inferred from a state change, and keep the chronology rule in §7 only. Define the selectable states of F14 and F19 as terms of the ontology (agreement states plus flow types plus `estimate` for need), and replace 'memorandum' with `mou` and 'reported' with the term that is meant.

findings.section: §3 Two match thresholds vs fusion §1 Calibrated language
findings.quote: about as likely as not or more, any confidence)
findings.issue: The default inclusive threshold counts every judgement at 'about as likely as not or more, any confidence'. Fusion §1 says a judgement that knows nothing is recorded as 'about as likely as not, very low confidence', and fusion §3 allows an 'undetermined' stance. Both therefore pass the inclusive threshold, so every candidate that no reader could decide joins the inclusive figure, and the range is inflated by undecided pairs. The same default would count a stance 'different' at that likelihood.
findings.why: The M3b headline figures are reported as a cautious-to-inclusive range. If the inclusive end absorbs all undecided candidates, the range is not informative and F11's test is hollow.
findings.fix: Define the threshold on the stance 'same' only, and set the inclusive default to 'about as likely as not or more, low confidence or more' (or exclude stance 'undetermined' explicitly). State this in fusion §3 so results §3 is an example, not a second rule.

findings.section: §8 Review minutes vs collection §10 and requirements DA6, Q15
findings.quote: minutes are attributed to the document class of the items.
findings.issue: Operation logs author minutes at M2 by 'document class'. The language document and collection §10 define document classes as frozen, living and series, which are assigned 'as a dated judgement' at M3a (DA6 is M3a). The documents extracted at M2 have no class at that time. Q15 and results §4 ask for spend and review time 'per document class', while AED-3 asks for cost per method. A parser, an assisted reading and a transcription have very different costs, and frozen, living and series do not separate them.
findings.why: The M2 sitting record and the M3b cost record would be keyed on a value that does not exist yet, and would not answer AED-3.
findings.fix: Key review minutes and spend at M2 on document type (DA3) and extraction method. In Q15 and results §4 say 'per document type and method'. If the class is wanted, add a rule that classes are assigned to the documents held at M2 before the M3b release.

findings.section: §9 Candidate triage (admit, context only) vs requirements DA12, extraction §7 out_of_scope
findings.quote: in scope as the requirements document defines it
findings.issue: Triage's 'admit' criterion refers to the requirements document, which defines no document-level scope: N2, N12 and N13 are exclusions, and the strict JETP scope of F13 is a counting scope. DA12 requires the ledger to hold operations of partner lenders that carry no JETP attribution, and pre-partnership milestones, while collection never says whether such a document is admitted or 'context only'. The 'context only' outcome ('kept and citable, not extracted') overlaps the extraction disposition `out_of_scope` ('held for context'). The language document splits the two lists, but does not say whether a context-only candidate is registered, so F2 and F27 do not know whether it is counted or checked.
findings.why: The admission criterion drives yield, the stopping rule and the recall estimate. Without it the two LLM readers cannot be given a stable question, and DA12's documents have no path into the register.
findings.fix: Add a short 'in scope' definition to requirements (a document is admitted when it states something about a JETP partnership, its projects, money, perimeters, parties or states, or belongs to the DA12 reference pool). State that 'context only' creates a registered document with the disposition `out_of_scope`, so there is one path and one count.

findings.section: §8 Unreachable documents are data vs §3 and §13, and requirements DA9, F8
findings.quote: declared but not published
findings.issue: Collection §8 lists 'declared but not published' among the reasons on the unreachable list. Collection §3 and §13 say 'not published' is 'a finding about the authority, not a gap in collection' and is 'not on the unreachable list'. DA9's test requires the list to include 'documents excluded by robots rules, terms of use or restricted access', but collection §1 lets a single fetch of a known document go ahead despite robots rules, and §8 has no 'excluded by robots or terms' reason. F8 says to keep 'not published, blocked, unreadable, not sought and loss of visibility distinct', but collection's verdicts and reasons include only some of these.
findings.why: A reviewer cannot tell from the documents which entries make up the unreachable list that the release must contain.
findings.fix: Delete 'declared but not published' from §8's reasons, or define it as a document (not an authority) that another document says exists. Reword DA9 to match the §8 reasons. Add the missing F8 terms ('unreadable', 'not sought', 'loss of visibility') to collection or drop them from F8.

findings.section: §4 Search channel classes vs §1 Structured search channels and requirements DA10, F19
findings.quote: CRS and IATI records, as pointers to documents
findings.issue: Structured reporting is in the campaign's fixed frame, and §4 says every class must be 'searched at least once per country and language before the stopping rule may fire', so it is an M3a condition. Yet the principle on structured channels, DA10, F19 and extraction (comparator records) are all [M3b]. Ontology and extraction §6.2 also treat comparator records as lines read 'in bulk' at M3b, while DA10 says they are 'held ... beside the documentary statements, never merged'. Collection does not say whether the M3a search of the class reads the records or only lists them as pointers.
findings.why: The M3a stopping rule and the recall estimate include or exclude a class, and the work at M3a changes by a whole channel.
findings.fix: Say in collection §4 whether structured reporting is searched at M3a for pointers only (then CRS and IATI records are read at M3b) and tag that row. Align DA10 and the ontology entry on whether comparator lines are in `lines` and how counts exclude them.

findings.section: §7 Traceability rate vs requirements F19 and results §2
findings.quote: **Traceability rate.** The share of claims examined that are traced
findings.issue: The same label names two rates. Collection §7 and Q10 define it as the share of secondary trackers' claims traced to a primary document (M3a). F19 and results §2 also require 'a public traceability rate' for 'the matching to CRS and IATI' (M3b), which has another numerator and denominator. Results §4's collection record does not list either.
findings.why: A release would carry an unlabelled rate, and a reader cannot tell which population it covers.
findings.fix: Name them apart ('tracker traceability rate' in collection, Q10 and the release's collection record; 'matching coverage rate' in F19 and results §2) and define the second one in fusion §5 or results §2.

findings.section: §4.4 F16 and the §9 table
findings.quote: known only by the year of a report is an interval ending at the report date,
findings.issue: F16's test needs the rule 'a milestone known only by the year of a report is an interval ending at the report date'. The table names 'Extraction § observations; Ontology; Fusion § 4' as its homes. Extraction §11 only gives the timings printed ('No date is invented'; 'approved in 2024' gets the year's bounds). Fusion §4 is Occurrence, not timelines. No document derives event bounds from a report date.
findings.why: The F16 test cannot be passed or failed by the specification as written, and the M3b results would each invent a rule.
findings.fix: Add the derivation to extraction §11 or to a fusion section (for example: an event stated without its own date gets upper bound equal to the report date and an open lower bound), and correct the F16 row of the requirements table.

findings.section: Whole specification (index, status lines, requirements §2.1, ontology, storage, presentation, language, operation)
findings.quote: Tracker: ticket 1703
findings.issue: The author's rule is no ticket numbers or dates in specification text, but they appear throughout: ticket numbers and PR numbers in the index (1703, 1707, 1708, 1709, 1710, 1711, PR #1596 to #1598), dated status lines ('Status: draft for author review, 2026-09-30'), 'until 2026-09-30' in requirements §2.1, 'ticket 1702' and 'ticket 0880' in ontology, 'ticket 0858' and 'PR #1492' in storage, and ticket links in presentation.
findings.why: These dates and numbers go stale and are the only reference that a reviewer can not resolve from the specification itself.
findings.fix: Move them to attic/ or to the ticket log, and keep only the section and rule identifiers in spec text.

findings.section: §3 What a statement carries (Verbatim fields, Classification) and §4 What becomes a statement (prose)
findings.quote: The list of field names is declared once per document at extraction, and every statement of that document conforms to it.
findings.issue: Walk of newsletter issues 8 and 13 and Decision 1009 (the spike): the statement shape is list-shaped and the spec has no shape for prose. §4 says 'Prose is extracted when it asserts something in scope', but §3 still wants a per-document field list, a closed classification and an own status word with an axis. The spec does not say who declares the field list. In the spike it was always the reader (4 of 4 lists), and one changed field name moved Decision 1009 from 57/59 kept to 13/46. Two issues of one series got different field names, so every cross-issue pair read as a change. `unclassified` was never used in 88 statements, so targets became `quota` and ministries became `named_item`. The walk also showed: the speaker of a quoted assertion is named in §4 but has no place in §3 or in the `lines` columns (news item and newsletter item #12 'Đại diện IPG và GFANZ'); and the record already holds 261 hand-made prose lines (146 `claim-N` lines, 115 `line-1160-...` lines) whose label is a composed summary and whose locator is a paraphrase. Not handled by the spec.
findings.why: About 100 of the 115 pending documents are prose or semi-prose: 13 newsletters, 27 project pages, 10 official news items, 4 annual-report pages, 2 secondary news items, the progress PDFs. The field list decides what is kept and what can be compared across issues. Left to the reader, it makes extraction unstable, replay meaningless and restatement impossible.
findings.fix: Add a prose statement shape to §3. (1) The label is the verbatim anchored span. (2) Typed value spans sit inside it under fixed generic fields: `amount_span`, `count_span`, `date_span`, `party_span`, `speaker`. (3) The field schema is fixed by the method version per document class or series and never proposed by the reader. `line-field-specs` is then keyed by class, not by document, for prose. (4) Add a `speaker` column to `lines` (as printed). (5) Grow the closed list by decision with `target`, `event` and `decision`, and make `unclassified` an explicit value the checker scores (the checker states its stance on the classification). (6) Own status is copied only when printed in a status position, never from a verb. (7) Declare how the 261 hand-made lines are handled at replay: re-extracted as quote plus locator and superseded under §9, or kept under a named legacy method.

findings.section: §6.3 Assisted reading (locator check, checker order); jetp-ledger-storage.md §1 (locator rule)
findings.quote: it must resolve, and the text there must contain the proposed label and values. A proposal that fails is rejected before any further check, and the rejection is recorded.
findings.issue: The locator check is undefined and mis-ordered (spike problem 2, not handled). The spec fixes no window, no normalisation and no rule for page furniture. Storage caps a prose anchor at 'at most 80 characters', which LLMs miscount. A label can be non-contiguous in the text layer: issue 8's count of 44 was split by a footer box and rejected. Planted-control rejections moved 6 → 5 → 3 with the window definition alone. Rejections are made before the checker, so the checker never sees them, and 22 of its 28 'missed' items in Decision 1009 v3 were the pipeline's own rejections, shown to the author without the reader's proposal. The folio is required ('the printed folio when one exists') but no rule detects it. In the record, 185 of 13,092 locators already exceed 80 characters, and the 261 hand-made lines have paraphrase locators that cannot resolve.
findings.why: This check is the gate of Traceable to bytes (F1) and of the planted-item control. Until it is defined, a correct statement can be rejected and an incorrect one admitted, depending on the implementation. It also inflates the author's missed-item queue.
findings.fix: (1) The reader proposes a verbatim quote and never writes a locator. Code derives the locator: PDF page index, plus a start anchor and an end anchor of at most 80 characters each, found by whitespace-normalised match over the text layer after declared page-furniture removal. The match must be unique, else an occurrence index is added. The printed folio is optional, recorded only when the adapter reads it. (2) The check is: the normalised quote is found in the text layer. Over-long anchors are trimmed by code, not by the LLM. (3) New order: reader → locator derivation and check → one repair call to the reader for failures → checker sees every proposal, failed ones marked. (4) The 'missed' list is de-duplicated mechanically against proposals and rejections. (5) State whether the 80-character limit applies to the anchor or to the whole locator, and whether the validator enforces it.

findings.section: §6.3 (author's queue) and §4 (declared extraction scope); jetp-operation.md §7.2
findings.quote: The author sees only the proposals on which reader and checker disagree, the items the checker says were missed, and a random sample of the proposals they agree on, all sorted by likelihood and confidence.
findings.issue: Projected on the 115 pending documents, the spike gives 7,000 to 12,000 proposals and 58 to 210 author hours, with the missed-item list the largest share. Operation budgets 100 items per run and 3 hours per week at 30 seconds per item; the spike measured 1.5 minutes per disagreement or missed item. The two documents cannot both hold. Defer-on-budget makes `deferred` the dominant M2 outcome, and deferral still counts as a disposition. The spec also does not say who declares the scope of a one-off prose document, so the reader's scope creep (ministry task lists read as `named_item`, targets as `quota`) enters the queue. 'Every item' is undefined for prose.
findings.why: C1 says no design rule may require the author to review every item of a class, yet the missed-item rule does. The M2 promise ('works on every document held') is not reachable at this rate without a mechanical filter.
findings.fix: (1) Replace the checker's 'missed' list, for prose, with a deterministic coverage control: every amount, count or date token in the in-scope text must lie inside some statement span, else it is listed as missed or excluded with a reason. The checker's missed items then only supplement it. (2) Make scope mechanical for one-off prose: in scope means carrying a typed value span, or heading such spans. (3) Where the text prints a sum relation (for example 557 + 78 + 93 = 728), check the typed spans against it (§4 printed totals, currently applied to no assisted reading). (4) State the expected queue per document class, as C1 requires, in §6.3, and make the author's unit a per-document stratified sample with a floor and a cap. (5) Reconcile the 100-item and 30-second figures with the measured rate, or say which wins.

findings.section: §10 Document classes (series row); jetp-extraction.md §2 (Edition) and §8 (Restatement, Pairing across snapshots)
findings.quote: each issue found is its own document, linked by `edition_of`; the series' publisher and stated periodicity are recorded
findings.issue: Newsletter issues are neither editions nor re-fetches, and restatement must be judged per value within printed bounds (spike problem 3, not handled). Restatement is defined only between snapshots of one document, matched by 'item and verbatim content'. Holdings walked: 13 MOIT newsletters (issues 8 and 13 both print the 44-project list; 0 of 7 pairs came out as restatements; 'hơn 10 tỷ' → 'trên 11 tỷ' and '728 triệu' → 'trên 700 triệu' are rounded or bounded repeats), 7 ZAF quarterly reports (one titled 'revised'), 4 cumulative ZAF grants-register editions, Decision 458 succeeding Decision 1009, and the 2025 Indonesian progress report re-listing the 2023 plan appendix. `documents.edition_of` is empty for all 392 documents and `relations` holds no `edition_of` row. The ontology defines `edition_of` only as 'succeeds a previous edition'. Key-less pairing is tagged M4 in §8 although the series are already held; 2 of 7 LLM pairings were false at 'likely' or above.
findings.why: OBS-5 (late report versus development), LP-2 (how official accounts changed) and F4's persistence-not-corroboration all depend on this. As written, the ledger calls every repeat of a stable count a change. Six issues repeating one count would also read as corroboration by a non-independent publisher.
findings.fix: Separate three things. (1) `issue_of`: a serial's member, with periodicity, no claim of succession. (2) `edition_of` for a re-issue or updated version of the same publication ('revised' quarterly, Decision 458 over Decision 1009); the progress-report-over-plan case is neither and gets no document relation. (3) A line-level `restates` relation judged per typed value: same value, or a value within the bounds a printed qualifier gives ('trên', 'khoảng', 'hơn'), is a restatement, otherwise a change. M2 needs only the `issue_of` or `edition_of` row. Key-less pairing for held series is M3b via the fusion proposers with the author seeing every pair; the M4 tag in §8 is limited to pairing across newly collected snapshots. No M2 requirement consumes pairing: F4's M2 test covers snapshots of one document.

findings.section: DA3 Document types; jetp-extraction.md §6.1 and §6.3
findings.quote: Repeated series get a dedicated parser; one-off documents get an assisted reading with row-by-row review.
findings.issue: Walk of an ADB project page with cumulative disbursements and of the ZAF justenergytransition.co.za project pages: the pages are neither an issue series nor one-off. Among the 115 pending there are 27 HTML project pages (11 from justenergytransition.co.za, 3 from adb.org, 3 from jetp.moit.gov.vn, and single pages from afd, kfw, worldbank, afdb, omvg and others) plus 15 HTML data portals. Each publisher's pages share one template across different projects. DA3's test ('each document extracted by a dedicated parser belongs to a repeated series') would forbid a template parser, which sends these 27 pages to the LLM route and its review cost. The spec also has no statement shape for a record page (labelled fields plus a description): §4 has list items and prose only.
findings.why: The route decides about 40 documents and most of the review load. It also decides the shape of the most common pending type, the project data sheet that carries the financing figures OBS-1 and SP-2 need.
findings.fix: Add a third route, a template parser: one parser per publisher template, eligible once three documents share it, refusing on landmarks like any parser. Reword the DA3 test to 'belongs to a repeated series or a template family'. In §4 add: a record page (data sheet) is one item statement for its subject, its labelled fields are the verbatim fields, and its free-text description follows the prose rule. Observations split per measure at M3b.

findings.section: §8 Dated snapshots and restatements (New bytes)
findings.quote: A later retrieval that returns different bytes forms a new snapshot, which is extracted in full, as if for the first time, under the same declared scope.
findings.issue: The only document of the 369 with two snapshots is zaf-ntcsa-transmission-plans, whose two retrievals are 9 seconds apart and return different bytes (218f5f97… and 69ebf776…). This is a page that differs per request (a nonce or timestamp), not a dated revision. Under §8, the second snapshot is extracted in full, yielding a full set of 'restatements' or, if a furniture line changes a statement, phantom changes. Every refetch of any of the 175 held HTML snapshots would do this, and each needs review. Fusion §3 names the timestamp page only as a document-level `same_as` proposer, not for snapshots of one document. The F4 and §13 item 6 machinery therefore has no real M2 instance and will be tested on a fixture.
findings.why: Without a rule for content-equivalent snapshots, refresh at M4 floods the ledger with false restatements. At M2 the one living-document case is misclassified, and F4's M2 test meets no genuine change.
findings.fix: Add a snapshot-equivalence rule to §8: if the normalised text layer (declared furniture removed, adapter version fixed) of a new snapshot equals an earlier snapshot's, nothing is extracted and the retrieval is recorded as a whole-snapshot restatement of the earlier one. Both byte-sets stay citable. Say in §13 that F4's M2 test is met by a fixture plus this document.

findings.section: §3 Verbatim fields; jetp-ledger-storage.md §1 (line-field-specs)
findings.quote: under the publisher's own field names as printed. The list of field names is declared once per document at extraction
findings.issue: The holdings contradict the rule in two ways. (1) `line-field-specs` for idn-cipp-2023-cpr-mirror, idn-jetp-progress-report-2025 and both Senegal annex documents share one parser-chosen list (`technology_group`, `priority_tier`, `estimated_investment_usd_mn`, `ruptl`), including for Senegal; these are not printed headers. (2) vnm-rmp-2023's spec is the union of at least three tables' headers ('No.', 'Name of Project', … 'No', 'Name of plant/construction', … 'Project name, task group'). Consequences: replay (Q1) shows a difference on every field of roughly 2,300 lines; the admission check that rejects a statement whose fields 'disagree with its document's declared field list' is vacuous for a union; the §11 check that the scale is 'one the statement or its heading prints' can never pass for `estimated_investment_usd_mn`, an invented name.
findings.why: Q1 (replay with zero unexplained differences) and the M3b value check both depend on field names that mean what the publisher printed. A union list also defeats the field-list check of §12.
findings.fix: Key the field list by (document, table), not by document. Allow a parser-declared, versioned mapping from printed header to field name, and keep the printed header (with its unit and scale wording) in `line-field-specs` beside the mapped name. State that the scale check reads the printed header, and that replay treats a rename covered by the mapping as explained.

findings.section: §3 (own status word and axis); jetp-ontology.md §4 (crosswalk)
findings.quote: The shared status is never assigned here; it lives only in the crosswalk.
findings.issue: The same §3 bullet has extraction copy 'the axis it belongs to', while the ontology says each own status 'maps through the crosswalk to at most one axis' and the `status-crosswalk` row carries the `axis`. So who sets `own_status_axis` at extraction is open. The spike's reader put 'Phê duyệt' on `project_stage`, giving an axis to the verb of a decision. In the record, 2,677 lines carry axis `delivery` and 1 carries `money`, including the ZAF register's letters 'A. Planned' to 'D. Completed' and comparator lines. Replay will flag them or bless them depending on an undefined rule.
findings.why: Assigning an axis at extraction is an interpretation that contradicts 'Extract, do not interpret', and it is wrong on prose. It also makes the column unreplayable.
findings.fix: Define `own_status_axis` at extraction as the printed column or heading name that carries the status word (for example 'Status'), empty otherwise and always empty for prose. The shared axis exists only in the crosswalk (M3b). State how the 2,678 axis values already in the record are explained at replay.

findings.section: §5 JSON and structured records, §6.2, §13; jetp-requirements.md DA2, DA10, Q1
findings.quote: [M2 for the documents held; the comparator records of CRS and IATI, M3b]
findings.issue: Of the 13,092 lines of record, 10,452 (80 %) are comparator records: OECD CRS 8,032, IATI 1,301, World Bank 1,119. They sit in `data_portal` documents (83 CSVs among the snapshots). DA2 counts them among the 254 documents 'already extracted (13,089 statements from 253 snapshots)', and Q1 requires replay of all of them at M2. Yet the extraction and DA10 tags say comparator records are M3b. The spec does not say whether replay, the bulk-run statement of §6.2 and the Q3 red test cover these 10,452 lines at M2. It also does not say what a later draw of the same query is (a new document per country-year slice, as the ids suggest, or a new snapshot of one living document).
findings.why: The boundary decides whether 80 % of the M2 replay is in scope, and whether the ingestion run needs a positive control (§12 lists none for ingestion runs, though §10 says replay binds them).
findings.fix: In §13 and DA2 state that the held CRS, IATI and World Bank snapshots are read at M2 by an ingestion run and replayed, and that 'comparator, M3b' means only new draws and their use in results (DA10). Add an ingestion-run control to §12 (a record count that disagrees with the printed or API total is rejected). Say that a later draw is a new snapshot of one living document.

findings.section: §5 Language, translation and summaries; jetp-extraction.md §6.4, §7 (deferred)
findings.quote: A scan with no text layer (the Vietnamese decision of 2026 is one) is read by transcription, and each of its lines names the transcription as its method and version
findings.issue: Storage §5 makes transcription an M2 rule for the scan, while extraction §7 allows `deferred` ('a scan awaiting transcription') and §15 says 'transcribed or deferred'. The scan is Decision 458, the updated implementation scheme and the newest Vietnamese plan (23 pp, 149 characters of text, language unknown in the register). If it is deferred, M2 is accepted with the current Vietnamese plan having no statements. §6.4 says 'the same automatic check of locators applies', but for an image there is no text in the bytes to check against; checking an OCR region against the same OCR text proves nothing.
findings.why: M2 acceptance and OBS-1 for Viet Nam both depend on it, and F1's test ('the printed text at the locator supports it') cannot be run by the automatic check for a scan.
findings.fix: Decide one rule. Preferred: Decision 458 is transcribed at M2, because it is one document. For any scan, the locator is page plus region; the automatic check is agreement with a second recogniser of another family on the region, or else a human check of the image for every statement, and the author's sample is of the image. The language is set by the operator when the text layer cannot detect it (DA5). If deferral is allowed instead, storage §5 must say 'or deferred' and the M2 acceptance must name this document.

findings.section: §2 (Document deduplication, Language extracted in a translation pair) and §7 (duplicate); jetp-fusion.md §3 Documents
findings.quote: nearly identical text with the same page count: a re-export, or a web page whose timestamp changes on every visit.
findings.issue: Walk of the mirror and translation cases (idn-cipp-2023 with its mirror, sen-investment-plan-l4 with its mirror, sen-annex8-project-analysis with the official-host copy, vnm-rmp-2023 in English and Vietnamese). The clear answers are the mirror rule ('the member already extracted stays canonical') and the translation rule. Not clear: (1) `same_as` is asserted for near-identical text, but the spec does not say what happens to the values that differ between members; a corrected figure in a re-export disappears (the member is `duplicate`, 'its statements are those of the canonical member'). (2) A translation pair is taken as equivalent, with no check that the non-canonical member holds no item or total the canonical one lacks. (3) A document that reproduces part of another (an annex published alone and in a bundle) has no relation and no disposition, so it is extracted twice. (4) The three held document `same_as` rows are status `candidate`, which storage §1 says is 'not in force'; yet §2 makes their outcome a precondition of extraction. Also, the canonical default 'the publisher's own address' can name a member with no snapshot (sen-investment-plan-annex8-official failed with an SSL error).
findings.why: F3 promises 'one set of statements and no added corroboration' for mirrored and translated documents, which holds only when the members are really equal. Otherwise numbers silently vanish or double.
findings.fix: (1) A `same_as` between non-identical bytes must record a diff of numeric tokens and row counts; a differing pair is not `same_as` but a revision or a separate document. (2) Apply the same check to a translation pair (printed totals, row counts, number tokens); on mismatch extract both or record them as distinct. (3) Add a document relation `part_of` (excerpt or annex): extract the part once, from the publisher's copy, and record the other scope as covered. (4) The canonical member must be one that holds a snapshot. (5) State that the pending document judgements are made, and in force, before the first run (§13 item 1).

findings.section: §5 LLM readers and the checking rule (long documents); jetp-extraction.md §3 (Ordinal) and §6.3
findings.quote: A document longer than the reader's context is split into parts with their own scope, as extraction § 6.3 provides; the largest held PDF has a text layer of about 950,000 characters
findings.issue: Twelve pending documents exceed 100,000 characters and the ZAF plan runs to 304 pages; at about 110 statements per call, splitting is routine, not exceptional. The spec does not say how parts are cut, nor what a part inherits. Open points: ordinals ('counted from one, in reading order') are per snapshot but parts are read independently; a group heading or method note that conditions rows in a later part is not seen by that part's reader; an item spanning a part boundary is lost or doubled; printed-total controls are defined per part but totals often cover the whole list; §6.3 lets the reader propose locators, so collisions across parts are possible ('no two statements claim the same place').
findings.why: Every large plan and report (the main body of the M2 review) goes through this path. Wrong seams produce missing or duplicated statements that no check looks for.
findings.fix: Add a chunking rule to extraction §6.3. Code cuts parts at structural boundaries (heading or page). Each part's call carries the governing heading chain and method notes as context. Adjacent parts overlap by one page, with seam items de-duplicated by derived locator. Ordinals and line identifiers are assigned by the pipeline after merging in reading order, never by the reader. Totals are checked at the boundaries the publisher prints.

findings.section: §4 (page furniture out of scope; prose attributed to its speaker) and §11 Timings
findings.quote: Navigation, boilerplate, legal notices, contents pages and repeated page furniture are out of scope unless the extraction declares otherwise.
findings.issue: Walk of newsletter issue 13 and of a news item. The item 'Ngày 27/3' has no year. The masthead carries it, but the reader's scope excluded the masthead as page furniture, so §11 ('a date printed elsewhere in the snapshot and governing the statement … names the statement it was read from') has no statement to name. The register already holds the issue's published_date, and §11 also says 'No date is invented'. Separately, for a news item that quotes an official or a bank, the publisher is the newspaper, the speaker is the quoted party, and there is no field for the speaker (see the statement-shape finding). Reuters or IEEFA pieces on Cirebon and de-dieselisation are admitted `secondary_news` and so extracted.
findings.why: Timings (F16) and attribution (the outcome 'quote a dated statement attributed to its publisher') both depend on context that the default scope throws away.
findings.fix: Make a dateline, masthead or issue period a mandatory `heading` statement whenever any statement of the snapshot carries a partial date. Allow year completion from the register's published_date or the series issue period only as flagged context, with precision and bounds stated, when no dateline statement exists. Add `speaker` (as printed) to the statement (see the shape finding).

findings.section: §4 measures (flow), timings; jetp-fusion.md §4 Occurrence
findings.quote: A repeated cumulative balance is not a new movement.
findings.issue: Walk of an ADB project page that states 'disbursements to date as of <date>'. A cumulative-to-date figure is a position, not a movement, but the ontology types money only as `flow` with `period_start` and `period_end` or a single `event` timing ('A point flow has one `event` timing'). There is no way to state a cumulative figure, so it will be read either as a point flow on the as-of date (a movement on that day) or as a period with an invented start. Fusion §4 and §7 (opening, movements, closing) need the two told apart to apply their own rule.
findings.why: OBS-1 ('disbursed, as of which date') and the gaps between financial states (F19) rest on these figures. Misreading cumulative as a movement double-counts disbursement across successive snapshots of the same page.
findings.fix: Add to the ontology a typed cumulative figure: a measure `cumulative_flow` (flow_type from the IATI list) with one timing role `reporting_cutoff` as the as-of date and no start. State in fusion §7 that it is a closing position candidate and never a movement. Add a check to extraction §11: a statement printing 'to date' or 'cumulative' must be read as that measure.

findings.section: §11 Reading statements into observations (How many); jetp-ledger-storage.md §1 (rates)
findings.quote: A statement yields zero, one or several observations, one per measure it prints.
findings.issue: Walk of the ZAF Investment Register: each row prints 'Amount: Pledged' (for example USD 2,280,000), 'Total US$' (2,280,000) and 'Total ZAR' (40,150,800) for the same pledge. By §11's rule it yields three `amount` observations; storage says a publisher's own conversion is a `rates` row citing the line. The extraction document never mentions it. Also note that the row mixes funders in a cell ('Funding Partners', 'Implementing Entity') and carries a footnote on the signing date (asterisk on the header), for which the heading-statement rule applies.
findings.why: The register is the largest documentary source of amounts. Reading three amounts per row triples every sum by construction and breaks F14 and F15.
findings.fix: Add to §11: a column the publisher derives from another by a printed rate is not a measure. The reading rule for the series declares which columns are original and which are derived; each derived column becomes a `rates` row citing the line, or nothing if the rate cannot be recovered. Add a red test: a row with three money columns yields one `amount`.

findings.section: DA5 Languages
findings.quote: English, Indonesian, Vietnamese and French.
findings.issue: The register holds one document each in Japanese, Chinese and German (idn-jica-mrt-north-south-2023, sen-genertec-ouarkhokh-chinese-2026, sen-giz-ped2-awards-2025), 59 of 392 with no language, and 13 with no document type. DA5's test only counts unknown languages and says nothing about these three. The checker rule ('whatever that language is') and the choice of reader do not cover them.
findings.why: The M2 acceptance test 'no document has an unknown language' would pass or fail on an arbitrary reading of the list, and three documents may end in no path.
findings.fix: State in DA5 either that the three documents get a recorded disposition naming the language (`unreadable` with format and language) or that the list of handled languages is extended by decision. Say that the register has a type for every held document at M2.

findings.section: Walk summary (no change proposed)
findings.quote: A report is held under the publisher's address and a partner's mirror, with the same bytes.
findings.issue: Where the specification gives a clear answer, on the nine held types I walked. (1) South African investment register (embedded JS table): parser route, printed summary rows as controls, hidden rows recorded, publisher's own status word kept, heading for the footnote rule. (2) Indonesian plan appendix with capacity lines: items as statements, technology headings as `heading` groups, capacity and cost as two observations, mirror handled by the canonical rule. (3) Senegal plan annex of submissions: `submission` and `evaluation` classes fit; long French labels kept as printed. (4) Data portal export (CRS, IATI, World Bank CSV): bulk ingestion, run-level review. (5) JavaScript portal bundle: `no_extractable_content` or literal read. (6) Generic byte stream that is a PDF: format from bytes. (7) Mirror: one extraction, `duplicate` on the other. (8) Translation pair: one language extracted. (9) Truncated or empty bytes: `unreadable`. Unclear or unhandled cases are the findings above.
findings.why: So that the review does not reopen rules that the walk shows to be sound.
findings.fix: None. Keep these rules. The findings above are the places where the walk did not get a clear answer.

findings.section: 1. Tables and rules (tables lines, line-referents, relations; no disposition table)
findings.quote: `lines` | `line_id` | country, sha256, locator, ordinal, label, classification, own_status, own_status_axis, own_sector, groups, recorded_at, notes
findings.issue: The M2 table for D2 cannot hold what the M2 rules of other documents require of a statement. `lines` has no method, method_version, adapter version, checking reader, author decision, hidden-cell flag, status or supersedes column. There is no table at all for dispositions (kind, reason, who, method, when), which extraction section 7 requires, which the pending list depends on, and which F2, F5 and DA2 test. Extraction sections 3, 5, 7 and 9 and F1, Q4 and Q17 all need these columns. Extraction section 9 and fusion section 2 also say a misread statement is superseded and stays readable, but only `observations` carries status and supersedes.
findings.why: F1, F2, F5, Q1, Q4 and Q17 are M2 acceptance tests. The DDL and the admission step are written from this table, so as drafted they cannot store a method version, a disposition or a superseded statement. A builder would invent columns, which is what the specification is meant to prevent.
findings.fix: Add to section 1, tagged M2: (a) on `lines`, the columns method, method_version, adapter_version, checker_stance and decided_by, a hidden flag, status and supersedes. Keep the extraction-only fields in `lines` and give the reading-step record its own table. (b) A `dispositions` table (document_id or sha256, kind, reason, decided_by, method, method_version, decided_at, status, supersedes). (c) Update the language D1/D2 table lists to match.

findings.section: 7. Dispositions; 1. Principles; 15. Checks (and requirements F2, DA2; collection section 2; language 'disposition')
findings.quote: | A held document has no bytes. | Disposition `no_snapshot`. |
findings.issue: `no_snapshot` is defined for a document with no bytes, but held is defined as admitted with at least one retrieval that yielded a snapshot, extraction section 2 says extraction receives a held document with at least one snapshot, and language restricts disposition to a held document or snapshot. A held document with no bytes is a contradiction. The 23 registered documents with no snapshot (DA2) are therefore outside every rule that could give them the disposition F2 requires. Collection section 11 gives the same state a third name, 'a recorded access outcome', which collection never defines and which is not among the retrieval statuses.
findings.why: DA2's test is 'every one of the 392 satisfies F2', and 23 of the 392 are in this state. The test cannot be decided as written. The disposition list, the pending list and the unreachable list are built on this distinction.
findings.fix: Decide one name and one owner. Suggested: for a registered document with no snapshot the record is collection's access outcome (latest retrieval status plus reason, on the unreachable list).
