Drop `no_snapshot` from extraction section 7, scope 'every held document' to 'every registered document has statements, a disposition, or an access outcome', and say so in F2, DA2, language and collection section 11.

findings.section: 7. Dispositions; 2. Scope and preconditions (pending list)
findings.quote: The input of every run is the pending list: the snapshots of held documents that have neither statements nor a disposition.
findings.issue: The pending list is defined on snapshots, but `duplicate`, `translation_not_canonical` and `out_of_scope` apply to a document, not a snapshot. Section 7 requires a snapshot-level disposition only for 'a document that is extracted'. A non-canonical mirror, the untranslated member of a pair or an out-of-scope document has snapshots with neither statements nor a snapshot-level disposition, so they stay pending for ever. That breaks the F5 test ('the pending set contains exactly' the new snapshot) and idempotence ('no disposition added'). Also, in the section 15 check the mirror whose bytes are identical shares its snapshot with the canonical member and is never pending, while a mirror with different bytes is.
findings.why: The pending list is the input of every M2 run and of every later run. If it never empties, the M2 completion test, the run's final state 'complete' (operation section 10) and F5 cannot be evaluated.
findings.fix: Define pending as: a snapshot of a held document that has no statements, no snapshot-level disposition, and whose document has no document-level disposition. State this once in section 2 and section 7, and add a section 12 control: a run over a duplicate document leaves the pending list empty.

findings.section: 7. Dispositions (deferred); operation sections 7.2 and 10; requirements 2.2 M2 row
findings.quote: A `deferred` disposition closes a document for the purpose of a run's completeness, but a run reports the deferred documents apart, by country and type, and a milestone's acceptance names them.
findings.issue: `deferred` counts as accounted for, with no ceiling, no permitted reasons and no deadline. The M2 definition of done is 'an extraction pipeline that works on every document held ... every document ends with statements or a recorded disposition'. Deferring everything that is hard satisfies it. The spike projects 58 to 210 author hours for the 115 pending documents against an operation budget of 100 items per run and 3 hours per week, so budget-driven deferral will be the normal outcome, not the exception. Operation section 10 lets a run be 'complete' and a release be built while documents are deferred.
findings.why: M2 acceptance and the Q5 and C1 bounds pull against each other, and this rule is the only valve. A reviewer cannot say met or not met for M2 or for 'works on every document held'.
findings.fix: Give `deferred` two permitted reasons (budget of the author's attention; awaiting transcription), require a named milestone and date for each, and add an M2 acceptance rule: a stated maximum share of held documents, or a named list, may be deferred. Also state that a release cannot be built while a deferred document is in its scope unless the release's coverage report lists it.

findings.section: 6.3 Assisted reading; 14 Open questions (and collection 9, operation 4 and 7.2, requirements Q5)
findings.quote: whether a floor should be fixed here, such as a share of agreed rows per document, is not settled.
findings.issue: The random sample of agreed rows that the author examines is the control that makes 'the checked statements are the record' and Q5 ('the share the author examined is stated and bounded') testable, and it has no rule. Extraction leaves it open. Collection section 9 says only 'a random sample of the agreements'. Operation gives a ceiling ('100 items presented (disagreements, missed items and random sample together)') and lets the author decide the size. A sample that is whatever is left of a cap of 100 is zero when disagreements fill the cap. 'Disagree' is also undefined: the spike had to invent 'stance other than right, or likelihood below likely', and it noted that items the checker lists as missed include the pipeline's own rejected proposals.
findings.why: Q5, Q17 and C1 tests cannot be run, and two runs of the same document can legitimately present very different review sets. Reader counts and sample sizes are method and must sit in one method document before the M2 assisted reading is built.
findings.fix: State in extraction 6.3 (referenced from collection 9 and operation 4): (a) 'disagree' = checker stance other than right, or likelihood below a named level, or the reader and checker locators differ; (b) the sample is a stated fraction of agreed rows with a floor per document; (c) the queue ceiling applies to disagreements plus missed items, and the sample is drawn in addition up to the floor. Close section 14.

findings.section: 3. What a statement carries (Classification); 1 (Append only); 6.1
findings.quote: When the extraction cannot tell, the statement waits for review rather than taking a default.
findings.issue: Classification is required on every statement, yet a statement may 'wait for review' without one. No state, column value or table says what an unclassified statement is: is it admitted, counted in the pending list, or covered by a disposition? Assigning the classification later is an edit, but section 1 forbids editing, and supersession is reserved for 'the ledger's own errors'. Section 6.1 says no partial set of statements is admitted from a failed extraction, which does not address a document with some unclassified rows. The spike found `unclassified` was never used in 88 statements, so the rule may be dead, but the gap would surface on the first document that does use it.
findings.why: Idempotence (Q2), the pending-list rule and append-only behaviour cannot all hold. A parser author has to guess.
findings.fix: Choose one: (a) classification may be null only on a statement with status `candidate`, resolved by a superseding row that is not an error correction (state this exception in extraction section 1 and fusion section 2); or (b) remove 'waits for review' and require the extraction to fail the document when a classification cannot be assigned. Add a section 12 control for the chosen rule.

findings.section: 1. Rules that the validator enforces (recorded_at rule); decision tables
findings.quote: Every record row in `lines`, `observations`, `timings`, `external-ids`, `rates`, `deflators`, `party-names` and every decision table carries `recorded_at`.
findings.issue: The table definitions do not meet this rule. `line-referents` and `relations` have `decided_at` and no `recorded_at`; only `adjudications` has both. `documents`, `retrievals` and `snapshots` have neither an admission time nor a triage or admission decision row, although fusion section 8 step 1 says a result at K admits statements 'and only if what they refer to was admitted too' and F10 is 'only what was admitted on or before K'. The as-of rule in the same bullet ('rows with `recorded_at` on or before K') therefore cannot be evaluated for identity decisions or for documents.
findings.why: F10, Q8 and every M3b result computed at a knowledge cutoff depend on it. The M2 document judgements (`same_as`, `edition_of`, `translation_of`) are `relations` rows, so the gap is already live at M2.
findings.fix: Add `recorded_at` to `line-referents` and `relations`, and say how it differs from `decided_at` (the ledger write time versus the judgement time, with K using `recorded_at`). Give documents an admission record: `admitted_at` on `documents`, or a triage row.

findings.section: 1. Rules that validator enforces (decision row in force); jetp-fusion.md sections 2 and 8; jetp-ontology.md section 5 (Revision)
findings.quote: an `accepted` row that any row supersedes is no longer in force
findings.issue: Combined with 'a terminal `candidate` row is pending and not in force', a proposed revision (a `candidate` row that supersedes an accepted one) removes the adopted judgement from force before the revision is adopted. Fusion section 2 says 'A revision that is only proposed does not take the place of what it would revise until it is itself adopted', and section 8 says 'a proposed revision leaves the judgement it would revise in place'. Ontology section 5 has the same gap: its revision rule uses the same accepted-terminal test.
findings.why: Any LLM or person proposing a revision would silently blank a match, a document fold or a term definition until the author accepts it, changing figures and extraction eligibility (a folded document would become pending again). The rule is tagged M2 because it governs document deduplication.
findings.fix: Say in storage and ontology that a row supersedes another only when it is `accepted` or `rejected`; a proposal is a `candidate` row with a separate `proposes` link, or it carries no `supersedes` until adopted. Add a validator test and a fusion check row.

findings.section: 1 (line-referents, relations, adjudications columns); 4. Matching records
findings.quote: `line-referents` | `referent_row_id` | line_id, referent_kind, referent_id, status, method, method_version, confidence, justification_line_ids, decided_at, decided_by, supersedes, notes
findings.issue: Fusion section 3 defines a judgement as a stance (the same, different, undetermined), a likelihood and a confidence on two calibrated scales, the statements it rests on, a quoted basis, who or what judged, method and version, and time. The decision tables hold a single `confidence` column, no likelihood, no stance and no quoted basis. `adjudications` has no method, method_version, confidence or justification. The match thresholds of F11 and Results section 3 ('likely or more, medium confidence or more') are conditions on two separate scales, so one column cannot carry them. Stance is also never mapped to `status` (candidate, accepted, rejected).
findings.why: F11, Q5, Q11 and every cautious and inclusive result at M3b depend on storing both scales. Redesigning the decision tables later means rewriting every migrated row.
findings.fix: Give all three decision tables likelihood, confidence, stance, basis (quote) and justification, and state the mapping stance to status. Add method, method_version and justification_line_ids to `adjudications`.

findings.section: 1 (coverage, dry-searches, retrievals.collection_method); jetp-collection.md sections 3 and 8
findings.quote: `coverage` | (referent_kind, referent_id) | review_status, checked_at, route, document_ids, notes
findings.issue: The M3a records are not specified. `dry-searches` and `decisions.md` are 'as today' with no columns. The round log, candidates, triage judgements, document class, known-item list, tracker claims and outcomes, and the discovery and newest-document dates have no table. `coverage` is keyed on a referent, but collection section 3 needs a terminal verdict (collected, not published, blocked, not applicable) for every expected authority and every listed project at M3a, before any project referent exists (projects are minted only at M3b by reviewed matches). `retrievals.collection_method` has four values against five rungs on the collection access ladder (no value for automated browser or web archive). There is no column for the site's robots or terms position or for the free registration used, both of which collection and F27 require.
findings.why: The M3a deliverable (recall estimate, unreachable list, verdicts) cannot be produced or audited from the declared tables, and the verdict key cannot exist at M3a.
findings.fix: Add M3a tables to section 1: `search-rounds`, `candidates` with triage judgements, `frame-entries` with verdicts keyed on an authority or listed-project key that is not a referent, `known-items`, `tracker-claims`. Add a rung column (five values) and a site-position column to `retrievals`, and a registration and public-route column to `documents`. Replace 'as today' with columns.

findings.section: 4. Occurrence (bullet 5) versus 7. Counting and accounts (Counting)
findings.quote: Signing, approval and disbursement are different measures, not successive states of one chronology.
findings.issue: Section 7 says the opposite: 'Financial states (need, announced, memorandum, approved, signed, disbursed) form a chronology, not additive categories: an aggregate selects one state explicitly.' F14 repeats the chronology wording. Ontology treats announced, mou, approved and signed as agreement states on one axis, and disbursement as a flow measure. So the section 7 list mixes states of the money axis with a flow measure, while section 4 says approval and signing are separate measures.
findings.why: F14's test ('no released figure adds signed and disbursed amounts') and the gaps between announced, signed, reported and disbursed (F19) depend on which of these are states of one axis and which are measures. Extraction section 11 picks measures on this basis, so different readers will pick differently.
findings.fix: Align on the ontology: states (announced, mou, approved, signed, cancelled, withdrawn) are values of the `money` axis on one agreement, disbursement and commitment are flows, 'need' is an `estimate` or `envelope` measure. Rewrite section 4 bullet 5 and the section 7 list and F14 accordingly, and add a check row.

findings.section: 1. Principles (Judgement, not automation) versus 3. Identity (Organisations; Documents proposers)
findings.quote: No rule below selects a value or merges two things on its own.
findings.issue: Section 3 contains rules that merge without a reading: 'An external identifier decides ... Two names that carry the same identifier are one organisation', case, diacritic and spacing variants are 'one party ... never two parties joined by an equality claim', and proposer 1 for both lines and documents is 'virtually certain'. A judgement may be made by 'a program', while principle 1 says fusion is done by 'LLM readers and people'. Requirements N4 ('No program admits a document, merges two identities, prefers a value') repeats the absolute wording, and extraction section 8 has a parser pair statements on a stable key as 'virtually certain'.
findings.why: Either the automatic rules are not allowed, or N4 and this principle are wrong. A reviewer checking N4 against the organisation rules gets 'not met'. The decision also determines how much of the 392-document dedup and the party authority needs a panel.
findings.fix: State the intended rule: a program may record a judgement only under a declared deterministic rule with a version (exact external identifier, identical bytes, case-fold), logged as a judgement by that method, revocable like any other. Reword principle 1 and N4 to 'no undeclared automatic action', and mark these rules explicitly as program judgements.

findings.section: 1. Principles (Discovery proposes, review admits) versus 9. Candidate triage (Checking at M3a)
findings.quote: No search, crawler, agent or watch admits a document on its own.
findings.issue: Section 9 says 'Where both agree, the triage outcome is in force. The author sees only the disagreements and a random sample of the agreements'. Admission therefore happens on LLM agreement, with the author reviewing afterwards on a sample. F7 ('admitted only by a recorded decision, never automatically'), N4 and operation section 4 (agents may not 'Admit a document') all read as a human act. Nothing says whether the two-reader agreement counts as the recorded decision.
findings.why: The M3a acceptance test (F7: 'absent from the register until an admission decision exists') and the freeze depend on who the decider is. A reviewer can reasonably find the same system either compliant or in breach of N4.
findings.fix: Say explicitly that the recorded decision may be a two-reader LLM judgement with the author's sampled review, and amend section 1, F7, N4 and operation section 4 ('agents' becomes 'coding agents and watches'), or require the author's acceptance of every admission. Also state how many sampled agreements an unreviewed admission may rest on.

findings.section: 3. The authority frame (verdict table) and 7. The recorded search; requirements F8
findings.quote: | not published | the recorded search (section 7) covered the search channels where it would appear and found none |
findings.issue: Section 7 defines 'the recorded search' only for a claim traced to a primary document: 'the publisher's own search channel, the partner disclosure search channel when a partner is named, and one general web search'. For a verdict on an authority, the publisher's own channel is the thing being tested, and a listed project has no partner named necessarily. So the coverage that justifies 'not published' is undefined, although collection section 3 calls it 'a finding about the authority'. F8 also says the Observer 'keeps not published, blocked, unreadable, not sought and loss of visibility distinct', but the terminal verdicts are only four and 'unreadable', 'not sought' and 'loss of visibility' have no place in collection. 'Not sought' would contradict a terminal verdict.
findings.why: Terminal verdicts gate the stopping rule (condition 1) and the published recall; 'not published' is a claim about a government, and it cannot be checked without a stated search standard.
findings.fix: Add a recorded-search standard for authorities and listed projects (which search channel classes, which languages, minimum rounds), separate from the claim standard. In F8, limit the terminal verdicts to the four collection values, and move unreadable, not sought and loss of visibility to the unreachable-list reasons or to M4.

findings.section: 7. The secondary-to-primary pass; 4. Search channel classes; 5. Stopping rule
findings.quote: The pass is a search channel class like the others: its admissions count as yield in the stopping rule.
findings.issue: The pass is not in the eight-row class table. It runs per claim, not per round (a round is one class, one country, one language). The stopping rule requires every class of the frame to be searched and the last two rounds to be in two different classes, but does not say whether the pass is a class for frame coverage or a round for the quiet tail. The table row for secondary trackers points to 'leads (section 6)', but section 6 is known items; the lead logic is in sections 1 and 7.
findings.why: Whether the pass counts changes whether discovery may stop in a country, and the check table cannot disambiguate. Two implementers will stop at different points.
findings.fix: Decide: either add the pass as a ninth class, searched once per country with its claims as the round, or say it is not a class and its admissions count as yield only in the round that admits them. Correct the cross-reference and add a check row.

findings.section: 4 (What a release contains), 6 (Metadata), 9 (Correction) versus 1 (Frozen bytes)
findings.quote: Once published, no byte of it is replaced, whatever is found later.
findings.issue: The metadata record is listed as part of the release ('The descriptor (section 5) and the metadata record (section 6)'), yet section 6 says the record lists 'the papers that cite it, added as they appear', and section 9 says 'the old release's metadata gains a pointer to its correction'. The check table says the bytes of `2026-11` 'are unchanged and point to the correction', which bytes that do not change cannot do. The descriptor pins 'every file of the package' by hash, so a changed metadata file breaks the hash the descriptor records. Section 9 also has an error found in a published release become `YYYY-MM-rN`, while F25 and section 9's next paragraph say an accepted report 'enters the next release'. The two paths are not reconciled.
findings.why: Q8 (frozen and reproducible) and F28/F29 test the frozen package, and the freeze-check at M3b can be failed by the very action section 9 prescribes.
findings.fix: Split the record into (a) an immutable in-package metadata file with no forward pointers, hashed in the descriptor, and (b) the deposit's own mutable record outside the package, where citations and supersession pointers are added and logged. Say which release an accepted report produces (`-rN` for a published release's error, next regular release otherwise) and align F25's test.

findings.section: 4.5 F9; 5 DA9; 7 C6 (M3a tests that name a release) and 2.2 milestone table
findings.quote: *M3a.* Test: both dates appear in the release and in every product citing it.
findings.issue: F9, DA9 ('Test: the release contains it') and C6 ('the release lists which bytes are redistributed') are tagged M3a with tests on a release. No release exists before M3b: the table puts 'a released dataset' in M3b, F28 is M3b, and Results section 13 makes the first release the M3b slice and tags the four dates M3b. The M3a deliverable, per the table and collection section 11, is a frozen register that publishes both dates 'with the register'.
findings.why: The M3a acceptance the author signs ('recall estimate and unreachable list before M3b starts') cannot be checked against these tests as written, and results and requirements disagree on when the dates and the redistribution list are first required.
findings.fix: Rewrite the three tests to name 'the frozen register and its publication' at M3a and 'the release' at M3b, or retag to M3b with an M3a register publication stated separately. Align Results section 4 and collection section 11.

findings.section: 6.4 Q20 (and section 9; presentation; operation section 11)
findings.quote: *M3b* for broken trails and pending judgements, *M4* for changes between runs. Test: a deliberately broken trail and a pending judgement both appear where the author looks
findings.issue: Section 9 assigns Q20 to 'Presentation; Operation'. The presentation document has no page, marker or list for broken trails, pending judgements or countries and documents without new statements. Operation section 11 puts the Observatory's 'supervision pages' at M4. Results puts the broken-trail check in the release build, not in a view. So the M3b part of Q20 is met by no document.
findings.why: Requirements section 2.4 says a requirement that no document meets is a gap in the specification. This is the OP-1 and OP-3 surface the author uses to supervise M3b.
findings.fix: Add to presentation (or operation) an M3b author's view: pending judgements sorted by likelihood and confidence, unresolved trails, countries and documents with no new statements. Keep the cross-run change flags at M4.

findings.section: 2 Observation (timings) versus 4 (Money observations; target) and 5 (Definition)
findings.quote: each with a role (`event`, `approval`, `reporting_cutoff`, `register_date`, `report_date`, `planned`)
findings.issue: Section 4 adds `period_start` and `period_end` for a flow, and the measure `target` is given 'a `target` timing'. None of the three is in the section 2 list. Extraction section 11 lists nine roles, and storage's `date_role` rule takes values only from terms in force. Section 5 says every date role is a `terms` row and the alignment test 'fails when a value listed in sections 2 to 4 is not a term in force'.
findings.why: Either the alignment test rejects the ontology, or the validator rejects `period_start`, `period_end` and `target` timings, which F16, flow intervals and account coverage depend on.
findings.fix: State the single closed list of date roles once (the nine of extraction section 11), reference it from the observation, money and measure sections, and have extraction cite it instead of repeating it.

findings.section: 2 Party and Asset; 3 Relations (party_in, role_in)
findings.quote: `funder`, `channel`, `promoter`, `implementing_entity`, `beneficiary`, `contractor`, `operator`, or publisher of a document
findings.issue: The relations that carry these roles are not specified. `party_in` is party to agreement only. `role_in` (party to project, asset, perimeter, document or line) has a closed role list of `lead_agency`, `coordinating_agency`, `guarantor`, `endorser`, `signatory`, `host`, `standards_body`, which does not contain promoter, implementing_entity, contractor, operator or beneficiary. Asset 'carries ... operator', and storage realises it as an `operator_party_id` column on `assets`, which the ontology does not mention and which bypasses the rule that parties attach by a reviewed decision. Project owner and operator have no place at all.
findings.why: F17 (owner, instrument, beneficiary and operator distinct), F20, SP-2 and the Organisations page depend on these roles. Storage's rule that cells listing several names are minted 'through `role_in` or `party_in` rows' has no valid role to use for a funder named in a project row.
findings.fix: Extend `party_in` to project and asset, or extend the `role_in` role list with promoter, implementing_entity, contractor, operator, beneficiary. Say which party roles attach to which subject kinds, and drop the `operator_party_id` column or declare it a derived view.

findings.section: 2 Party (party name forms); jetp-fusion.md section 3 Organisations; jetp-ledger-storage.md section 4
findings.quote: Exactly one form is preferred at a time
findings.issue: Three defects. (1) Form type conflates kind and preference: `preferred` is one value of the same list as `acronym`, `translation` and `former_name`, so the preferred form cannot also be recorded as an acronym (e.g. SENELEC). (2) Fusion says an acronym against its expansion is a real variant, settled 'in a result whose match threshold the judgement meets', which makes identity depend on the result, but storage section 4 says an accepted `same_as` physically folds the two parties and redirects the old identifier, for all results. (3) After a fold there are two `preferred` rows while the rule allows one.
findings.why: F12's tests (Senelec and SENELEC one party; PLN and Perusahaan Listrik Negara one party only by judgement) cannot be met consistently. Releases at cautious and inclusive thresholds would differ in which parties exist.
findings.fix: Make `preferred` a flag and keep form type a kind. Keep parties distinct with a threshold-dependent `same_as` judgement, and compute a merged view per result, with routes redirecting only after a cautious-and-inclusive-unanimous fold, or fold physically only for deterministic identifier and case-variant merges. State the preferred form after a fold.

findings.section: 5. Ontology tables; 0. Frame (versus jetp-spec.md Structure)
findings.quote: The ontology is data about the ledger's words, stored like the ledger itself
findings.issue: jetp-spec.md says documents 0, 2, 3, 4 and 5 'name no storage and no presentation'. Ontology section 5 defines tables with keys and column lists, file paths (`data/jetp/ontology/`), a DDL test and build outputs (Glossary, SKOS export), and the storage contract's own table list does not include the ontology tables. The one place that defines `terms`, `status-crosswalk`, `sector-crosswalk`, `perimeters` and `marker-coefficients` is a conceptual document.
findings.why: Author ground rule: conceptual documents name no storage. A DDL builder reading the storage contract will not find five of the M2 tables, and the statement in spec.md that conceptual rules are realised in a cited implementation document is false here.
findings.fix: Move the table definitions, paths, alignment test and export mechanics of section 5 to the storage contract (section 1 and 3), leaving in the ontology the conceptual rules (definition, traceability, revision, as-of) and a pointer.

findings.section: 2 Retrieval and Publisher; header status
findings.quote: how the two lists relate is a proposed schema change (ticket 1702)
findings.issue: The document is 'Status: in force' and the retrieval status rule is tagged [M2], but its closed list includes `not_published` and `not_applicable`, stated not to be outcomes of a fetch, and the relation to collection's verdicts is an open proposal. The authority category `secondary_source` is likewise awaiting rename. The alignment test (M2) checks these lists against `terms`, so the M2 DDL must freeze a list the text says is unsettled.
findings.why: `retrievals.status` and the terminal verdict are both built at M2 and M3a. Freezing a list with two non-fetch values forces a migration later, and the spec's own status line contradicts the body.
findings.fix: Decide before the DDL: retrieval status holds the ten fetch outcomes only, terminal verdicts live in collection's own list, and the rename of `secondary_source` is done or dropped. Remove 'proposed' wording from in-force text, or change the status line.

findings.section: 5. DA2 The documents held (and jetp-operation.md 7.1; jetp-ledger-storage.md section 3)
findings.quote: 254 already extracted (13,089 statements from 253 snapshots)
findings.issue: The population counts do not reconcile across documents. DA2 has 254 documents from 253 snapshots (one more document than snapshot) and 115 pending documents with a snapshot, implying at least 368 distinct snapshots if pending documents do not share bytes. Operation 7.1 measures 'the document store of record: 278 objects'. Storage section 3 says its tables 'hold about 8 000 rows today' against 13,089 statements in DA2. Cause not established (shared snapshots, objects versus snapshots, lines versus all rows, different dates), and no document says which.
findings.why: Q1 (replay of 254 documents), the DA2 test, the operation budget (derived from 278 objects) and the pending list (115 of 392) all hang on these counts. A count that moves between passes is an alarm.
findings.fix: Run one query on the register and store, publish a single reconciliation table (documents, distinct snapshots, objects in the store, statements, documents sharing a snapshot), and make DA2, operation 7.1 and storage section 3 cite it. Reword 'documents' versus 'snapshots' in DA2.

findings.section: 3. Relations (same_as and cites rows)
findings.quote: `same_as` (document) | document | document | one publication under two URLs or two exports; the lines belong to the canonical one
findings.issue: `same_as` has three rows with three meanings (document, line, and a generic 'any to same kind ... justified equality claim; does not choose a route'), and `cites` has a line row and an observation row with different ranges. Section 5 says a relation term states one domain and range and that the alignment test matches each value to one term in force. The document form canonicalises extraction, the generic form explicitly does not choose a route, and storage uses one `relations.relation` column for them.
findings.why: M2 relies on the document `same_as` for extraction eligibility. The validator cannot tell 'folds the document' from 'asserts equality' on the same relation value, and the terms test cannot match three rows to one term.
findings.fix: Use distinct relation terms (`same_document_as`, `same_item_as`, and a generic `equivalent_to`), or add a qualifier column and state the domain and range per term. Split `cites` likewise.

findings.section: Whole specification (reading-order table, milestones, Around); also language, ontology, storage, collection, presentation headers
findings.quote: Tracker: ticket 1703.
findings.issue: The ground rule is no ticket numbers or dates inside spec text. The spec index has ticket numbers and PR numbers in its State column, and the other documents embed tickets and dates in normative text: language and ontology (ticket 1702, 0870, 0871, 0880, dated decisions), storage (tickets 0858, 0873, 0885, 0833, key families named for tickets 0970 and 1160, dated amendments), presentation (0881, 0882, 0877, 0902) and requirements (dated status and the 'until 2026-09-30' note on DA). The State column also says Results is 'being drafted (ticket 1707)' and Operation is 'being drafted (ticket 1708)', though both documents are complete drafts.
findings.why: A reviewer cannot tell provenance from rule. Identifier families in storage are tied to ticket numbers that the spec then cannot drop, and state labels are stale, so the index misleads about what is reviewed.
findings.fix: Remove ticket, PR and date references from normative text and move them to the attic provenance pages. Keep the identifier family names without ticket numbers. Replace the State column with draft, reviewed or accepted, and fix the Results and Operation rows.

verdicts.reason: Quote is exact (extraction §5, l.213-214). The reading holds in part: locators are text anchors resolved 'through a named adapter version', the layer is discarded on adapter change, and the spike showed two adapters disagreeing on reading order. But 'silently' is wrong: §10 replay re-resolves every LLM-read locator against the bytes and its positive control must fail on alteration, and §9 already prescribes a reviewed old-to-new locator mapping when a method version moves locators. What is genuinely missing is the input that mapping needs: once the old adapter build is gone, the old layer cannot be regenerated, so the §9 mapping has nothing to compare against. Not a blocker (M2 builds and replays correctly today); a real horizon risk, cheap to close since 84 PDFs yield 11.65 M characters of text.
verdicts.better_fix: In §5 replace 'is discarded when either changes' with: the text layer of every snapshot that has admitted statements is retained (under DVC beside the bytes) with its adapter name, version and hash, recorded in the run report; a later adapter writes a second layer beside it and the §9 mapping is reviewed old-layer to new-layer. Pin the adapter by exact version in the environment lockfile the repository already has; do not add a container. Add one red test to §12: replay against a snapshot whose retained layer is deleted and whose adapter version is unavailable must fail loudly, not resolve against a fresh layer.

verdicts.reason: Quote is exact (extraction §6.3, l.318-319) and the checker does see only surviving proposals, so at M2 it ratifies rather than reads blind (fusion §3 makes blind reading M4). However 'the agree-but-wrong rate is unmeasured' is wrong: the random sample of agreed proposals the author decides on (§6.3, Q17) is precisely that measurement; what the spec lacks is a rule to stratify, compute and report it. The Bắc/Bác example is not evidence of checker credulity: those were matching judges, and 'extract, do not interpret' requires the misprint to be recorded as printed. The planted-item control does test recall and fabrication only, so a planted-misreading control is a legitimate shape-of-guard addition. Capping confidence at medium and rewriting Q5 are overreach: statements carry no confidence, and Q5's test is about panel composition.
verdicts.better_fix: Add to §12: the control document also carries a planted misreading (a transposed digit or altered value in a proposal handed to the checker) that the checker must flag; a checker that passes it is admitted. Add to §6.3 and the run report (operation §8): the author's decisions on the random sample yield the agree-but-wrong rate, computed per language and document class and stated in every run report and the M3b cost record. Leave fusion §3 confidence and Q5 unchanged.

verdicts.reason: Quote exists (collection §10). But the core claim, that no rule decides restatement versus corroboration across issues, does not hold: extraction §2 says an edition's statements are never merged, fusion §3 makes a pairing 'to one in another edition' a candidate match (M3b for lines), fusion §1 and §2 say a publisher repeating itself adds no corroboration, and storage §4 names the CIPP/progress-report edition relation as the M3b tier-2 test bed. The M4 tag in extraction §8 concerns snapshots of one living document, not series. M2 extracts each issue as its own document and needs no cross-issue pairing; the spike ran one because its brief asked. What survives is the two homes of `edition_of` (storage §1 `documents` column and §4 `relations` rows).
verdicts.better_fix: Drop `documents.edition_of` or declare it a derived cache of the `relations` row, so the relation has one home. Add one sentence to extraction §8: pairing statements across editions or issues is a candidate match of fusion §3 [M3b], not a restatement. Do not add `issue_of`: the ontology's `edition_of` ('succeeds a previous edition') already covers issues, and a new relation has no consumer before M4.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. `lines` (storage §1) carries no method, method_version or decided_by, while extraction §3, F1, Q4 and Q17 require them on every statement at M2 and storage tags the D2 tables M2; the ontology likewise puts method only on observations. No table holds the dispositions of extraction §7 (`deferred`, `out_of_scope`, `unreadable`, `no_extractable_content`, `wrong_content` have no home; `coverage` is keyed on referents), nor the reader/checker record of §6.3, nor the restatement and unpaired links of §8. Since the DDL generates the CSV headers, a coder cannot add these without changing the contract, and F1, F2, Q4 and Q17 are M2 tests against the record.
verdicts.better_fix: In storage §1 [M2]: add method, method_version, decided_by to `lines` (mirroring `observations`); add a `dispositions` table (document_id or sha256, kind, reason, method, method_version, decided_by, recorded_at, status, supersedes) under the in-force rule; add a `readings` table for each proposal with reader and checker outputs (proposal_id, line_id nullable, role reader|checker|author, llm_id, prompt_version, stance, likelihood, confidence, basis, cost, recorded_at, step_at_fault) to serve Q17; record restatement and unpaired as `relations` rows between lines (relation `restates`, and an `unpaired` marker row) rather than a new table. Tag the M3a tables (triage outcomes, document class, verdicts, round log, known items, tracker claims) with the collection fields, as the finding proposes.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. verdicts.better_fix: As proposed: 'registered' in extraction §1, §7, §10 and §13, 'held' only for having a snapshot; and one sentence in §2 or §7: a document-level disposition closes every snapshot of that document for the pending list. Fix the §15 row to 'A registered document has no bytes'.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. Extraction §3 defines `ordinal` as reading-order position counted from one; storage §1 mints `line_id` as `<document_id>-<table>-<ordinal>` 'in extraction order' and appends a missed row 'under the next ordinal'. An item missed mid-sequence gets a reading-order ordinal already taken, or an out-of-sequence one, and the `line_id` suffix and the `ordinal` column can differ. Replay (Q1) compares field by field and the admission step rejects renumbering, so the code must choose one meaning; storage is in force, extraction is draft. verdicts.better_fix: Adopt storage's meaning: `ordinal` is the mint counter in extraction order, never reassigned; delete 'in reading order' from extraction §3 and let the locator carry position. verdicts.reason: The quote exists, but the set already answers it: Q5 says LLM judgements 'are made without the author', C1's test forbids any rule that makes the author review every item, and fusion §3 lists 'a program, an LLM reader, a panel, a person' as distinct judges, so within the spec's vocabulary an LLM reader is not 'a program'. Define the selectable states as ontology terms: agreement states plus IATI flow types plus `estimate` for need; replace 'memorandum' with `mou`; define 'reported' as the amount a comparator record (CRS or IATI) reports, or drop it from F19 and the language document.

verdicts.reason: The logic holds: a judgement 'about as likely as not, very low confidence' is fusion §1's know-nothing case, and the inclusive default (any confidence) counts it; fusion §3 also allows an 'undetermined' stance, and a threshold on likelihood alone does not say which stance's likelihood it reads. Results §3 does, however, make the defaults the author's method choice set before M3b and its §14 check deliberately counts 'about as likely as not' at the inclusive end, so the confidence floor is a design call, not a contradiction. The stance point changes the threshold function.
verdicts.better_fix: State in fusion §3 that a match threshold applies to the likelihood of the stance 'same' and that 'undetermined' counts in no result; present the confidence floor of the inclusive default to the author as a decision with the know-nothing case as the argument for 'low or more'.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed that operation §8 keys minutes on the document class, which DA6 and collection §10 assign at M3a. But DA6's test requires every admitted document, the M2 ones included, to have a class by M3a, so a sitting logged at M2 per run and per document can be aggregated per class at M3b by join; the M2 record is not keyed on a missing value if it records document identifiers. verdicts.reason: Confirmed. Collection §9's 'admit' defers to a requirements definition of document scope that does not exist (N2, N12 and N13 exclude; F13 scopes counts); the nearest statement is extraction §4's relevance sentence. 'Context only' is 'kept and citable' without saying whether the document is registered, so F2 and F27 cannot tell whether to count it. This drives triage, yield and the stopping rule at M3a.
verdicts.better_fix: Add an 'in scope' definition to requirements §2: a document is admitted when it states something about a JETP partnership's projects, money, perimeters, parties or states, or belongs to the DA12 reference pool. Say in collection §9 that 'context only' registers the document and it receives the extraction disposition `out_of_scope`, keeping the language document's split between a candidate's triage outcome and a held document's disposition.

verdicts.reason: The quotes exist, but the premise (an author's rule against ticket numbers and dates in specification text) is not in the set and cannot be verified from it; the index deliberately carries ticket and PR references as state markers, and Q21 requires every rule to be 'reachable from' its decision record, which the ticket references serve. verdicts.reason: The quote is exact and the gap is real: §3 describes a list-shaped statement (per-document field list, ordinal in a sequence, storage line_id `<doc>-<table>-<n>`) and §4 only says prose is 'anchored on its own words, attributed to its speaker'; there is no place for the speaker in §3 or in `lines`, and `unclassified` is a review state in §6.1 but not a value the reader can answer. The finding overstates one point: §6.3 says the reader is *given* the declared field list, so the spec already implies the method declares it; the spike's reader-supplied lists were the spike's choice, not the spec's. It also under-reads §3: 'label as printed: the item's name or description' already fits 'the verbatim anchored span' for prose. Not a blocker: M2 code can be built under the existing rules with a fixed per-class field list; what is missing is the sentence that says so and the speaker/unclassified/legacy-lines decisions. The 261 hand-made lines are a genuine replay problem, covered under finding 1.
verdicts.better_fix: Narrow the fix to what the spec lacks. (1) In §6.3 state that the declared scope and field list are set by the method version per document class or series and never proposed by the reader; the storage key of `line-field-specs` stays per document, but the value is copied from the class. (2) In §4 add one bullet: for prose, the label is the shortest verbatim span that carries the assertion, and the fields are the class's fixed list (speaker as printed, date as printed, amount as printed), each a verbatim substring of the span; no typed value spans at M2, since typing is reading (§11, M3b). (3) Let the reader answer 'cannot classify' and make that the review-wait state of §3; grow the closed list by decision (`target`, `event`, `decision`) only after the author sees the cases. (4) The reader never sets `own_status_axis` (finding 7). (5) The 261 `claim-`/`line-1160-` lines keep their identifiers and are listed by replay as outside its reach under a named legacy method; a later re-anchoring supersedes them under §9 when the document is re-read. Drop `line-field-specs` keyed by class: the storage contract validates per-document headers and the record already holds 97 rows.

verdicts.reason: Quote exact. Three documents disagree on what a locator is: §3 'precise enough to be unique', §5 'a text anchor of a few words', storage §1 'a text anchor of at most 80 characters for prose', §6.3 'the text there must contain the proposed label and values' with no window or normalisation. The record already violates the storage rule (185 locators over 80 characters: 170 of the 261 hand-made lines plus 15 `Project heading:` locators), and the hand-made locators are paraphrases ('Table 4.3-2 p.72, Canada Clean Energy...'), which cannot pass §10's replay check for non-parser statements. So the M2 validator and the M2 replay, built as written, fail on the ledger of record and Q1's 'zero unexplained differences' cannot be met without a decision. That is what makes it a blocker; the checker order and the missed-list inflation (22 of 28 in the spike) are major and the spike documents them well. The finding's fix is sound and consistent with 'Traceable to bytes'.
verdicts.better_fix: Keep the proposed fix, with two adjustments. (a) State the rule once, in extraction §5, and have storage §1 cite it rather than restate the 80 characters: a prose locator is page index plus a start anchor and an end anchor, each derived by code from the reader's verbatim quote after whitespace normalisation and declared furniture removal, unique in the text layer or carrying an occurrence index; the folio is recorded only when the adapter reads it. (b) Say what happens to the record: locators admitted before the rule stay valid under their method version, replay lists them as outside its reach, and the validator enforces the new syntax on new lines only. Then the reorder (reader, derived locator, one repair call, checker sees every proposal with failures marked, missed list de-duplicated against proposals and rejections) follows in §6.3.

verdicts.reason: The textual conflict is real: §6.3 has the author see every item the checker says was missed, while C1's test says no design rule may require the author to review every item of a class. But the arithmetic is weaker than stated. The spike report says the author's review was simulated and that 1.5 min per item is an assumption ('estimated from the item counts'), not a measurement, so 'the two documents cannot both hold' is not shown; operation §13 already says 30 s is a default replaced by the logged rate. The 7,000-12,000 proposal projection inherits the spike reader's scope creep and the rejections-as-missed inflation that finding 1 removes. The budget-split-defer mechanism of §6.3 and operation §7 exists, and §7 requires the M2 acceptance to name the deferred documents, so the outcome is bounded and visible. What the spec lacks is the expected queue per document class that C1 asks for, and a bound on the missed list. The deterministic token-coverage control proposed is over-built and conflicts with the declared scope (not every number in a document is in scope).
verdicts.better_fix: (1) De-duplicate the missed list mechanically against proposals and recorded rejections (from finding 1). (2) Treat the missed list like the agreements: reviewed in full up to a floor, sampled above it, the floor stated per run. (3) State in §6.3 the expected queue per document class once the first sittings are logged, as C1's test requires, and note that the projection is re-made after the first ten prose documents. (4) Make scope mechanical for one-off prose only as a default the method version declares (a statement is in scope when it carries a printed amount, count, date or state about a partnership's project, money, perimeter, party or state), not as a token-coverage check. (5) Apply the printed-total control of §4 to assisted readings by asking the reader for the printed total as a `count` or `envelope` statement and comparing. Drop the '1.5 minutes measured' premise.

verdicts.reason: The quote is exact, but the reading conflicts with the set's own vocabulary and the issue is handled elsewhere. jetp-language.md defines edition as 'a publisher's successive issue (`edition_of`)', storage §3 calls the monthly grants register 'the monthly edition', and extraction §2 makes every edition its own document. Restatement in §8 applies only between snapshots of one document, so the spec does not 'call every repeat of a stable count a change' across issues: across editions there is no restatement judgement at M2 at all, statements are related by matching (fusion §3, 'relates a statement to one in another edition', M3b), the later position of the same publisher is judged in fusion §5, rounding bounds are carried in fusion §7, and 'a publisher repeating itself is not independent of itself' (fusion §1-2) prevents the corroboration the finding fears. The spike applied §8 across two documents where it does not apply. The M4 tag in §8 concerns key-less pairing of snapshots of one document, not editions. That `edition_of` is empty for all 392 documents is a data gap M2's precondition step (§2, §13 item 1) already requires filling, not a spec gap.
verdicts.better_fix: One gloss change: in ontology §3 define `edition_of` as 'a later issue or edition of the same publication or series', and in collection §10 say 'linked by `edition_of` (an issue of a series)'. No `issue_of` relation, no line-level `restates` relation, and no move of key-less pairing to M2. If the author wants restatement-across-editions as a result at M3b, it is a fusion §5 judgement on a candidate match, already provided.

verdicts.reason: Quote exact. The gap is in wording, not in the rules: extraction §6.1 ('where a publisher repeats one format') and §1 ('a parser is written for a publisher's repeated format once two or three of its documents are in hand') already admit a parser for a publisher's page template; only DA3's test says 'repeated series', which is narrower. The 27 pending project pages (11 justenergytransition.co.za, 3 adb.org, 3 jetp.moit.gov.vn) are real, and the record already holds 90 project_page lines and ADB project documents, so the shape question is live but small: §4's 'an item of a list is one statement' with the page's labelled fields as verbatim fields and the description under the prose rule is the natural reading. No third route is needed.
verdicts.better_fix: Reword DA3's test to 'belongs to a repeated series or a repeated format of one publisher' and add the words 'or a page template' to §6.1's examples. Add one bullet to §4: a record page (a project data sheet) is one item statement for its subject, its labelled fields are its verbatim fields under the printed labels, and its free-text description follows the prose rule. Nothing else changes.

verdicts.reason: Verified: zaf-ntcsa-transmission-plans has two `collected` retrievals at 05:55:43Z and 05:55:52Z returning different bytes (218f5f97..., 69ebf776...), and it is the only document with two snapshots. §8 as written extracts the second in full and pairs every item as a restatement or change, and the same will happen on every M4 refetch of a page with a nonce. F4's M2 test and §13 item 6 therefore have no genuine instance and the one instance held is mishandled. The proposed rule is small, deterministic and consistent with 'Identical bytes'.
verdicts.better_fix: As proposed, with one precision: the equivalence is on the text layer under a named adapter version and a declared furniture rule, recorded as a whole-snapshot restatement with the adapter version in its method, so replay can regenerate the verdict. State in §13 and in F4's test that the M2 test runs on a fixture plus this document, and that the fixture is a copy of a held snapshot with one value changed.

verdicts.reason: Verified in `line-field-specs`: idn-cipp-2023-cpr-mirror, idn-jetp-progress-report-2025, sen-investment-plan-annexes-mirror and sen-investment-plan-l4-mirror share one list (`technology_group`, `priority_tier`, `estimated_investment_usd_mn`, `ruptl`), which cannot be the Senegal annex's printed headers; vnm-rmp-2023's list is the union of three tables' headers ('No.', 'Name of Project', 'No', 'Name of plant/construction', 'Project name, task group'). Storage §1 says 'header as printed' and extraction §3 'under the publisher's own field names as printed', so the record contradicts the rule, replay (Q1) will show a difference on every field of those lines, the admission check against a union list is vacuous, and §11's scale check reads a name that prints nowhere. Not a blocker: §10 lets replay classify these as 'legitimate and explained', but that explanation has to be written once, as a rule, before the replay is built.
verdicts.better_fix: As proposed: key the field list by (document, table), which the storage line_id `<document_id>-<table>-<ordinal>` already anticipates; allow a parser-declared, versioned mapping from printed header to field name, keep the printed header (with unit and scale wording) beside the mapped name in `line-field-specs`, and state that the scale check of §11 reads the printed header and that replay treats a rename covered by the mapping as explained. Add that a mapping shared across documents (the Senegal annexes reusing the Indonesian names) is a defect to correct by a new spec row, not an explained difference.

verdicts.reason: The conflict is real but narrower than stated. The ontology's Line puts 'which axis that word belongs to' on the line [M2] and the storage `lines` table has `own_status_axis` [M2], so assigning an axis at extraction is the design, not a violation of 'extract, do not interpret'; the contradiction is with the crosswalk that defines the axis being M3b, and with the reader assigning it. The record's 2,677 `delivery` values come from the ZAF register parser's reviewed configuration and replay reproduces them, so they are not at risk. The live defect is the spike's reader putting 'Phê duyệt' on `project_stage`. The proposed fix would redefine the column as a printed heading name, breaking 2,677 rows, the ontology gloss and the crosswalk's `axis`.
verdicts.better_fix: State in extraction §3 that `own_status_axis` is set only by a parser's reviewed, versioned status list for its series (the crosswalk in waiting, adopted as `status-crosswalk` rows at M3b) and is empty for assisted readings, transcriptions and a person's reading until the crosswalk exists; an LLM reader is never asked for it. Say that replay reproduces the 2,678 axis values from the parser configuration.

verdicts.reason: Verified: 10,708 of 13,092 lines sit under `data_portal` documents, the CRS/IATI/World Bank draws among them. DA2 counts those documents among the 254 'already extracted' that Q1 must replay at M2, while §5 ('the comparator records of CRS and IATI, M3b'), §6.2 and §13 ('M3b extracts the comparator records') put them at M3b, and §12 names no control for ingestion runs although §10 binds them to replay. Whether 80 % of the M2 replay is in scope is undecided in the text, and the id family (`oecd-crs-energy-sen-2005-q-2026-09-28`, one document per slice and draw) settles the 'new document or new snapshot' question one way while the living-document class of collection §10 suggests the other. A one-paragraph decision, but one that sizes M2.
verdicts.better_fix: As proposed. State in §13 item 3 and DA2 that the held CRS, IATI and World Bank snapshots are read at M2 by the ingestion run of §6.2 and replayed, and that 'comparator, M3b' means new draws and their use in matching and results (DA10, F19). Add to §12 an ingestion control: the record count read must equal the count the API or file states, else the run fails. Decide the draw question in favour of what the record does today (a draw of a query slice is a new document dated by the draw, related by `edition_of` to the previous draw of the same slice), since a living-document reading would require re-keying the existing 10,452 lines.

verdicts.reason: Verified: storage §5 [M2] says the scan 'is read by transcription'; extraction §7 allows `deferred` for 'a scan awaiting transcription' and §15 says 'transcribed with the transcription named as method, or deferred with that reason'; vnm-decision-458-2026 is pending, an implementation_plan, with no language recorded, and it is the current Vietnamese instrument. The proposed second-recogniser-of-another-family rule is over-built for a single 23-page document.
verdicts.better_fix: Decide one rule and write it in both places. Preferred: Decision 458 is transcribed at M2 by a recogniser, its lines carry the recogniser as method and version, the locator is page plus region, and the check is the author's inspection of the image for every statement (23 pages is one sitting), which is the person-as-checker case §6.4 already allows; the language is set by the operator when no text layer can detect it (DA5). If deferral is chosen instead, storage §5 must say 'or deferred', and the M2 acceptance names this document and the reason.

verdicts.reason: Verified: the three document `same_as` rows are `candidate` (mirror_review), and both sen-investment-plan-l4 and sen-investment-plan-annex8-official hold no snapshot while their mirrors are extracted. But most of the finding is already handled: the canonical rule 'the member already extracted stays canonical' keeps the Senegal mirrors canonical; the candidate status is exactly what §13 item 1 ('deduplication applied') requires M2 to resolve before the first run; a differing value in a near-identical re-export is decided by the tier-4/5 judgement fusion §3 already requires before `same_as` is accepted; an annex extracted alone and again in a bundle is handled by the declared scope of §4, which may stop short of a part with a stated reason. The real residue is small: the default 'the publisher's own address is canonical' can name a member with no bytes, and nothing asks the judgement to look at numeric content.
verdicts.better_fix: (1) In §2, the canonical member is chosen among members holding a snapshot. (2) Add to fusion §3's document proposers that a `same_as` or `translation_of` judgement between non-identical bytes records the difference in row counts and numeric tokens as its quoted basis, so a re-export that changed a figure is judged `edition_of`, not `same_as`. (3) For an annex held alone and inside a bundle, the bundle's declared scope excludes the annex and names the document it was extracted from; no `part_of` relation. (4) One sentence in §13 item 1: the three pending document judgements are decided and in force before the first run.

verdicts.reason: Quote exact. Operation §5 sends context-length splitting to extraction §6.3, but §6.3 defines splitting only as a response to the author's review budget ('split into parts with their own scope') and says nothing about seams, inherited headings, items across a boundary, per-part totals or ordinals; §3 defines the ordinal per snapshot, which independent part readers cannot assign. Twelve pending documents exceed 100,000 characters and operation §7.1 gives a 947,000-character largest PDF, so every large plan goes through this path and no check of §12 looks at seams. The proposed rule is small and consistent with §3 (pipeline assigns ordinals) and §4 (an item over a page break is one statement).
verdicts.better_fix: As proposed, in extraction §6.3, with the seam de-duplication keyed on the code-derived locator of finding 1 (which this fix depends on) and with one red test in §12: a fixture cut so that an item straddles the seam yields one statement, and a printed total covering two parts is checked after merging, not per part.

verdicts.reason: The observation is right: the spike's scope excluded the masthead, 'Ngày 27/3' has no year, and §11 forbids inventing one. But the spec already has the rule: §4 says a method note that conditions a page is a heading statement grouping what it conditions, and page furniture is out of scope 'unless the extraction declares otherwise', so a dateline that governs every item is in scope under the existing method-note rule; the spike's scope declaration missed it. The speaker is covered under finding 0. Year completion from the register's `published_date` would break §11's rule that a timing names a statement; a dateline heading statement is the correct route and needs one example, not a new mechanism.
verdicts.better_fix: Add 'a dateline, masthead date or issue period' to the examples of the method-note bullet in §4, and add to the declared-scope rule that page furniture carrying a date, issue number or publisher name that governs the statements is in scope by default. No completion from the register.

verdicts.reason: The gap is real: nothing in the ontology or extraction §11 says how 'disbursed to date as of D' is typed, and ADB project pages holding such figures are in the register. But the vocabulary already covers it without a new measure: a flow carries `period_start` and `period_end` (ontology §4, storage §1), timings admit precision `unknown`, and fusion §7's reconstruction counts a movement inside an interval only when 'its earliest possible date is after the opening', so a flow whose start is unknown can never be counted as a movement and serves as the closing candidate the adjudication roles `opening`/`closing` already exist for. The finding's 'invented start' does not follow; an unknown-precision start is the spec's own device. A new `cumulative_flow` measure and a word-triggered check in §11 add vocabulary with no consumer that the existing rule does not serve.
verdicts.better_fix: Add one sentence to extraction §11 (Timings): a figure printed as cumulative or 'to date' is a flow whose `period_end` is the as-of date and whose `period_start` has precision `unknown`, bounded below by the agreement's earliest printed date when one exists. Add one to fusion §7: such a flow is a closing-position candidate and never a movement. Add the case to §15's checks.

verdicts.reason: Verified: the ZAF register spec prints 'Amount: Pledged', 'Total US$' and 'Total ZAR', and the storage `rates` rule says a publisher's own conversion is a `rates` row citing the line. But the record already reads exactly one `amount` per register line (257 of 257, in the original currency), and §11's reading rule per series is 'a versioned mapping from a series' verbatim fields to measures', which chooses which columns become measures; nothing forces three. The ambiguity is the sentence 'one per measure it prints', which a naive reading rule could take literally. A one-sentence clarification and a red test settle it; the mixed-funder cell and the footnote are already handled by storage §1 and §4's heading rule.
verdicts.better_fix: Add to §11 (How many): a column the publisher derives from another by a printed rate is the same measure, not a second one; the reading rule declares which column is original, and each derived column becomes a `rates` row citing the line when the rate can be recovered, else nothing. Add the red test 'a row with three money columns yields one `amount`' to §11's checks.

verdicts.reason: The languages are verified (ja, zh, de: idn-jica-mrt-north-south-2023, sen-genertec-ouarkhokh-chinese-2026, sen-giz-ped2-awards-2025) and 59 documents have no language, but the count of documents without a type is 2 (two local-record pilot manifests), not 13. verdicts.reason: Verified. storage §1 line 42: `lines` has no method, method_version, status or supersedes; no table anywhere holds dispositions, yet extraction §3 requires method+version, checker and author decision on every statement [M2], §5 requires a hidden flag and adapter version, §9 supersedes a misread statement, §7 makes a disposition a record with kind, reason, decider, method, version, time [M2], and F1/F2/F5/Q4/Q17 test these at M2. verdicts.reason: The quote and the contradiction exist: extraction §7 opens with 'a held document or snapshot', §15 says 'a held document has no bytes', held means at least one snapshot (collection §2). But the 23 documents are not 'outside every rule': F2 lists 'no snapshot' explicitly as a disposition reason and DA2's test is decidable through it. Collection §11's 'recorded access outcome' is a third name for the same fact. Wording, not design.
verdicts.better_fix: Reverse the proposed direction. Keep `no_snapshot` (F2 and DA2 name it, and it is an M2 list). Widen extraction §7's opening and language's 'disposition' row to 'a registered document, or a snapshot of a held one'; change §15's 'held' to 'registered'; make collection §11 say the recorded access outcome is the disposition `no_snapshot`, whose reason cites the latest retrieval's status. Dropping the kind would reopen F2, DA2 and language for a rename.

verdicts.reason: Quote exact (extraction §2 line 114). The strict reading does leave snapshots of `duplicate`, `translation_not_canonical` and `out_of_scope` documents pending, and F5 and §12 both define pending on snapshots. But §7 says 'every snapshot of a document that is extracted ends with ... a disposition of its own', which implies snapshots of non-extracted documents are covered by the document-level disposition; the intent is inferable, the sentence just does not say it.
verdicts.better_fix: The proposed fix is right and cheap: define pending once in §2 as a snapshot with no statements, no snapshot-level disposition, and whose document has no document-level disposition; cite it from §7, §12 and F5; add the §12 control that a run over a `duplicate` document leaves nothing pending.

verdicts.reason: Quote exact (extraction §7 line 379). The valve the reviewer asks for already exists in the same sentence: 'a milestone's acceptance names them', so the author accepts M2 with the deferred list in view, and operation §7.2 already bounds the review budget. What is missing is that requirements 2.2's M2 row and DA2's test never mention the deferred list, so a reviewer reading requirements alone would pass an all-deferred M2. The budget arithmetic (58-210 hours at 3 h/week) is a planning fact, not a spec defect.

Add to requirements 2.2 (M2 row) and DA2's test: 'the list of deferred documents, by country and type, is part of what the author accepts'. The two reasons are already the two named in §7. For releases, results §4 already carries a coverage report: say there that deferred documents in scope are listed on it.

verdicts.reason: Quote exact (extraction §14). 'Disagree' is undefined anywhere: §6.3 has the checker state 'whether the proposal is right, with a likelihood and a confidence', and the spike had to invent a rule. The sample has no floor; operation §7.2 caps disagreements, missed items and sample together at 100, so the sample can be zero. Q5's and C1's tests are runnable as written (the run states its size), so the 'why' overstates, but the M2 assisted-reading code cannot be built the same way twice without these two definitions, and Q17's reference answers depend on them.
verdicts.better_fix: In extraction §6.3: (a) 'disagree' = checker stance other than right, or likelihood below `likely`; (b) the sample is a method parameter with a stated default (a share of agreed rows with a floor per document), recorded in the run report; (c) keep operation's 100-item cap over the whole queue and apply the existing split-or-defer rule when disagreements + missed items + the floor sample exceed it. Do not draw the sample 'in addition' to the cap: that breaks C1's stated queue size. Also de-duplicate the checker's missed items against rejected proposals (spike §5.2). Close §14.

verdicts.reason: Quote exact (extraction §3 line 141). Classification is required and append-only forbids editing, so a stored unclassified statement has no path. But the text's own methods already review before admission: assisted reading's proposals go to the author before admission (§6.3), and a parser's output is reviewed as a diff before admission (§6.1). Read that way 'waits for review' is a pre-admission state, and no ledger row is ever unclassified. The sentence just does not say so, and the DDL builder needs to know whether the column is nullable.
verdicts.better_fix: Neither option proposed. State in §3 and §1: a statement is admitted only with a classification; 'waits for review' means the proposal stays in the run's review queue (assisted reading: the author's queue; parser: the document is not admitted, consistent with §6.1's no-partial rule). DDL: `lines.classification` NOT NULL. No candidate status on `lines`, no document failure.

verdicts.reason: Verified: storage lines 47-48 give `line-referents` and `relations` decided_at, decided_by, supersedes and no recorded_at; only `adjudications` (line 52) has both; the rule at lines 101-105 says every decision table carries recorded_at and defines the as-of state on it [M2]. Document relations (`same_as`, `edition_of`, `translation_of`) are `relations` rows at M2 (storage §4), so the contradiction is live at M2. `documents` has no admission time.
verdicts.better_fix: Add `recorded_at` to `line-referents` and `relations` and define it as the ledger write time (K uses it) against `decided_at`, the judgement time. For documents, do not add `admitted_at`: admission at M3a is a triage judgement (collection §9) that is defeasible, so it is a decision row with status and supersedes; for the documents held at M2, extraction §3 already dates holding by the earliest retrieval that yielded the snapshot.

verdicts.reason: Verified: storage lines 89-96 say a terminal candidate is not in force and an accepted row that any row supersedes is not in force, so a candidate that supersedes an accepted row leaves nothing in force. Fusion §2 and §8 say the opposite. Ontology §5 repeats the accepted-terminal test. Operation §4 has agents 'propose supersession', so proposals will exist. At M2 a proposed revision of an accepted `same_as` would make the folded document pending again (extraction §2).
verdicts.better_fix: Simpler than a `proposes` link: in storage §1 and ontology §5 write 'an accepted row is no longer in force once a row that supersedes it is itself accepted or rejected; while its only successor is a candidate, the accepted row stays in force and the candidate is pending'. Add a validator test (candidate over accepted: accepted still in force) and a fusion §9 check row.

verdicts.reason: Verified: line-referents and relations carry one `confidence` column; adjudications carry verdict, status, decided_at, decided_by, recorded_at, supersedes, notes and no method, method_version, confidence or justification. Fusion §3 'The judgement' [M2] requires stance, likelihood and confidence, quoted basis, statements, method+version. Storage §4 speaks of 'the panel's stance-and-confidence rule' with no column for stance or likelihood. Milestone is M2, not M3b: the document judgements are `relations` rows and fusion tags the judgement shape M2.
verdicts.better_fix: Add likelihood, stance and basis to all three decision tables, keep confidence, and add method, method_version and justification_line_ids to `adjudications`. Do not map stance to status: status is workflow (candidate, accepted, rejected) and stance is content; an accepted 'different' row is meaningful (it stops the pair being re-proposed). Tag the columns M2 for `relations`, M3b for the rest.

verdicts.reason: Verified: storage lists `coverage` keyed on a referent, `dry-searches` and `decisions.md` 'as today', nothing for rounds, candidates, triage judgements, document class (DA6, M3a), known items or tracker claims, though collection says the record of searches is storage's business. `collection_method` has four values (the data today: script 320, local-record 87, browser-session 16, browser-manual 3) against five rungs in collection §8. Map the four existing `collection_method` values onto the five rungs explicitly and add the web-archive rung (or state that an archive copy is a retrieval whose host party is the archive, rung 5). Add a document-class column or relation for DA6. Add site_position on `retrievals` and registration/public_route on `documents`.

verdicts.reason: Both quotes exist (fusion §4 bullet 5 vs §7 'form a chronology', F14 repeats §7). The wording contradicts, but the intent of both is the same (never add, never infer one from another) and the ontology §4 money axis already settles which are states (announced, mou, approved, signed, cancelled, withdrawn) and which are flows (disbursement etc.); extraction §11 reads measures from the ontology, so readers will not pick differently.

No milestone or build impact.

verdicts.reason: Verified: fusion §1 'no rule below selects a value or merges two things on its own' and N4 'no program ... merges two identities', against §3 'an external identifier decides', case variants 'never two parties', proposer 1 'virtually certain', and 'who or what judged (a program ...)'. The pieces to resolve it exist (threshold per result; storage §4 registers identical-bytes as a `same_as` candidate; decided_by may be a script), but they leave the M2 question open: a candidate row is not in force, so both members of an identical-bytes pair stay pending and are extracted twice unless someone accepts it, and nobody is named.

Add to fusion §3: a program records a judgement only under a rule the author adopted by version (identical bytes, same external identifier, case or diacritic variant), recorded `accepted` by that method under that decision in `decisions.md`; every other program or LLM proposal is `candidate` until the checking rule of operation §5 or the author accepts it. Then storage §4's 'registered as a same_as candidate' applies to tiers 2 and up only.

verdicts.reason: Quotes exist, but the question 'does two-reader agreement count as the recorded decision' is answered in collection §9 ('Where both agree, the triage outcome is in force ... counts for the register once in force') and endorsed by Q5 ('admission judgements ... made without the author', M3a) and C1. Operation §4's 'agents' are the development agents of that section, not LLM readers; operation §5 explicitly covers LLM triage. What remains is a letter-level clash between N4/F7 and Q5 inside requirements.
verdicts.better_fix: Wording only: N4 'No program, and no rule without a recorded judgement, admits a document ...'; F7's test 'until an admission decision, which may be a checked LLM judgement under Q5, exists'; operation §4 'development agents'. The sample-size question belongs to finding 4, not here.

verdicts.reason: Quote exact. Collection §7's recorded-search standard (publisher's own channel, partner disclosure when a partner is named, one general web search per language) is written for claims, but it applies to an authority with 'publisher's own channel' read as the authority's portal, which is the test of publication, not circularity; the stopping rule's condition 1 already requires every class searched before any verdict stands. F8's five states are things to keep distinct across the system, not five verdicts: F8 itself lists the four terminal verdicts; unreadable is an extraction disposition, not sought is the cap-stop's unmet conditions (§5 Backstop), loss of visibility is M4.

verdicts.reason: Verified: collection §7 says the pass 'is a search channel class like the others', the §4 table has eight classes without it, the 'secondary trackers and news' row points to 'leads (section 6)' but §6 is known items (the lead logic is §1 and §7), and the pass runs per claim across countries while a round is one class, one country, one language. verdicts.reason: Verified: ontology §2 Party names funder, channel, promoter, implementing_entity, beneficiary, contractor, operator; `party_in` is party-to-agreement only; `role_in`'s closed list (lead_agency ... standards_body) has none of the project or asset roles; Asset 'carries ... operator' and storage puts `operator_party_id` on `assets`, bypassing the rule that parties attach by decision. verdicts.reason: Verified on all three points: `preferred` is a value of the same form_type list as `acronym` (ontology §2, storage party-names), so a preferred acronym cannot be typed; fusion §3 makes a party merge result-dependent ('in a result whose match threshold the judgement meets') while storage §4 folds physically on an accepted `same_as` and redirects via `routes`, which no cautious result can undo; after a fold the retained party holds two `preferred` rows against 'exactly one'. F12's two tests cannot both hold consistently.
verdicts.better_fix: Make `preferred` a flag column and keep form_type a kind. Fold physically only under the deterministic rules fusion §3 already calls 'never two parties' (same identifier, case or diacritic variant), with the retained party's preferred form stated by supersession of the other's; every other party `same_as` stays a judgement, and each result computes its party view at its threshold. Reserve `routes` for identifiers retired in a published release.

verdicts.reason: Verified: jetp-spec.md says documents 0, 2, 3, 4, 5 name no storage; ontology §5 defines five tables with columns, a path, a DDL test and exports, and its own header says 'no storage'. But the claim that a DDL builder 'will not find five of the M2 tables' is false: storage §1 line 13-14 cites `data/jetp/ontology/` and ontology §5 by pointer, and tags the ontology tables M2 at line 62. A structural inconsistency, not a build gap.
verdicts.better_fix: Lighter than a move: have jetp-spec.md state the one exception (the ontology tables are defined in ontology §5 and incorporated by the storage contract), or move only the table rows and the path to storage §1 and leave definition, traceability, revision and the alignment test in the ontology.

verdicts.reason: The quote exists and the document is 'in force', but the open item is already owned by ticket 1702, the list is the current manifest's, and terms revise by supersession. Verified in the data: today's 426 retrievals use only collected, blocked, fetch_error, not_modified, http_error, invalid_content and missing; no row carries `not_published` or `not_applicable`, so dropping the two values later costs no row migration. Naming an open ticket in an in-force document is provenance, which jetp-spec.md's 'Around' section endorses.
verdicts.better_fix: None needed in the specification; note on ticket 1702 that no retrieval row uses the two verdict values, so the DDL can freeze the ten fetch outcomes and 1702 removes two terms at zero migration cost.

verdicts.reason: Measured on the worktree tables (documents.csv, retrievals.csv, snapshots.csv, lines.d, documents.dvc). Reconciles: 392 documents, 369 with a snapshot, 369 distinct sha256, 23 without, 254 documents with lines from 253 snapshots because exactly one snapshot is shared by two documents (the ontology's mirror case), 115 pending. Does not reconcile: lines are 13,092 not 13,089; the DVC store holds 278 objects (282 MB, matching operation 7.1) against 369 snapshots, 91 short, with 87 retrievals of method `local-record`, cause not established; storage §3's 'about 8 000 rows' is stale (13,092 lines; 121,844 CSV rows in all). The 91 matter beyond bookkeeping: the M2 validator rule 'the bytes exist in the store' cannot pass for a line whose snapshot has no object.
